AO Exam — Master Combined Study Guide

CGHS + CS(MA) Rules, 1944 — Complete Master Guide

Batch 1 (CGHS) + Batch 2 (CS(MA)) — Combined Without Omission, Fact-Checked, DA-Updated

This master file merges the two companion batches — CGHS (the scheme for the ~80 CGHS-covered cities) and CS(MA) Rules, 1944 (the statutory rules for non-CGHS areas) — into a single document with zero content omitted from either source file. Both batches were independently fact-checked against primary MoHFW/DoPT/DoE sources before merging (see the verification notices retained inside each section below). All DA-linked figures have been updated to reflect the current DA/DR rate of 63% (effective 1 July 2026 — Department of Expenditure OM No. 1/2(i)/2026-E.II(B) dated 29.10.2026 raised DA from 60% to 63%); these are formula-based thresholds that move at every DA revision, so the computed rupee figures are flagged as dynamic, not final.

🌐 Official Web Review — MoHFW/CGHS Current-Order Check (19 July 2026)

The latest-order layer was reviewed against the official CGHS portal, the official MoHFW Central Services (Medical Attendance) page, and the Government-hosted copy of the 16.02.2026 MoHFW OM. The guide retains the 13.05.2026 parents/parents-in-law clarification, 16.02.2026 HoD ceiling update, 16.09.2025 transgender-dependent amendment, October 2025 CGHS package-rate revision, 20.09.2023 AMA-fee revision and 01.12.2020 hearing-aid rates. Dynamic portal figures are identified as snapshots.

Source-control rule: MoHFW/CGHS portal pages and the actual OM text control over third-party summaries. Any order issued after 19 July 2026 must be checked and inserted as a dated delta.

✅ CGHS — Verified Correction & Official-Source Notes (July 2026)

Verified against official sources: MoHFW/CGHS portal (https://cghs.mohfw.gov.in/); MoHFW OM F.No. 5-16/CGHS(HQ)/HEC/2024 dated 03.10.2025 (package rates effective 13.10.2025); MoHFW OM 28.06.2024 + 24.09.2024 (referral SOP); OM 27.06.2024 (card guidelines); MoHFW OM 16.09.2025 (transgender dependents); OM 08.11.2016 (Rs.9,000+DA dependency); DoPPW OM 13.03.2026 (FMA for UPS); MoHFW OM 12.04.2023 (consultation/room rent); OM 01.12.2020 (hearing aids); OM 09.09.2024 (neuro-implants); OM 22.01.2025 (respiratory devices); OM 18.03.2024 (75+ health check); OM 27.01.2022 / 17.02.2022 (digital card); staffnews.in / govtstaff.com / official press reproductions.

  • All CGHS package-rate figures (consultation ₹350/₹700, room rents ₹1,500/₹3,000/₹4,500, ICU ₹5,400, Oct 2025 revision framework) confirmed against 03.10.2025 OM.
  • Referral SOP clauses (A–E, 70+, emergency, chronic) confirmed against 28.06.2024 r/w 24.09.2024.
  • Parents/parents-in-law chronology (03.03.1987 → 26.07.2023 → 28.03.2024 → 13.05.2026) and transgender dependent (16.09.2025) confirmed.
  • Card rules, contribution tables (7th CPC, w.e.f. 01.01.2017), FMA, ward entitlement, MRC ceiling (₹10 lakh per 16.02.2026 — applies to ALL MRC claims incl. permission/post-facto approvals; HoD settles without IFD consultation) cross-checked against current official orders.
  • CGHS is an executive scheme governed by OMs/guidelines — it has no statutory numbered sub-rules. All entitlements live in Government Decisions/O.M.s, not in invented sub-rule numbering.
🏥 PART 1 — CGHS (Batch 1): establishment, family definition, parents/parents-in-law, cards, contributions, referral, Oct-2025 package rates, senior provisions (70+ & 80+), digital, Q&A ⚖️ PART 2 — CS(MA) Rules 1944 (Batch 2): Rules 1–11, GDs, Insurance, Pensioner exclusion & latest amendments

Who can join CGHS — 5 km rule removed (OM 17.09.2026)

OM F. No. Z.16025/227/2026/CGHS-III/EHS(8421134) dated 17.09.2026 — eligibility of serving Central Government employees for CGHS (immediate effect). It refers to OM No. C.14012/02/2018/CGHS-III/DIR dated 06.04.2018, under which CGHS coverage of serving employees was restricted to those residing / working within a 5 km radius of a CGHS Wellness Centre.

  • The geographical (5 km) criterion is totally dispensed with.
  • One-time option: serving employees residing / posted outside the earlier geographical coverage or in a city not covered by CGHS, who are on CS(MA) Rules solely for that reason, may opt to become CGHS beneficiaries, subject to other eligibility conditions and payment of the prescribed CGHS contribution.
  • Mandatory CGHS: serving employees residing or posted within the CGHS-covered area, i.e. the limits of the district headquarters where a CGHS Wellness Centre is situated, are mandatorily covered under CGHS and cannot opt out in favour of CS(MA).
  • Conditions of the option: one-time, final and binding; applies to all dependants (no splitting between the two systems); the employee keeps paying the CGHS contribution irrespective of residence / posting; no simultaneous claims under CGHS and CS(MA); no TA/DA for treatment or medicine procurement under CGHS rules; an undertaking that benefits will not be availed under both systems (inadmissible benefits are recoverable).
  • Employees who do not opt continue under CS(MA) Rules, 1944. False, incorrect or suppressed information attracts disciplinary action under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and recovery.

Effect on the exam answer: “CS(MA) applies where CGHS does not” is now only the default. A serving employee outside a CGHS area may choose CGHS once, irrevocably, for the whole family.

CGHS final-claim time limit — 6 months (OM 01.06.2020)

CGHS OM File No. 1-60/2017-CGHS/C&P/EHS (e-signed 01.06.2020) — “Revision of time limit for submission of final claims for reimbursement of medical expenses under CGHS”.

  • Earlier CGHS guidelines: 3 months. Revised to 6 months.
  • Only cases where bills are submitted after 6 months from the date of completion of treatment / discharge from hospital need to be taken up for condonation; the power of condonation and other terms are as in OM No. S.14025/8/99-MS dated 25.05.1999.

Correction made: the guide’s “CGHS = 3 months; CS(MA) = 6 months — different!” is obsolete. Both CGHS and CS(MA) final claims are now 6 months (CS(MA): 6 months from discharge / treatment; 1 month from discharge where an IPD advance was drawn). No later revision was found; confirm on the CGHS site before quoting.

Read from the published text of the OM.

Financial powers — CGHS (OM 25.06.2026)

CGHS OM No. Z.15025/14/2/DIR/CGHS dated 25.06.2026 (Director, CGHS; IFD concurrence Dy. No. 1029 dated 18.06.2026) — “Revision of delegation of financial powers for settlement of medical reimbursement claims and grant of permissions/ex-post facto approvals in respect of pensioner CGHS beneficiaries and other eligible beneficiaries, including serving CGHS employees”. It revises the powers under the earlier OM No. Z.15025/79/2/DIR/CGHS dated 05.10.2016.

C. Permissions / ex-post facto approvals

  • (i) Elective treatment / investigations in non-empanelled hospitals, diagnostic labs or imaging centres for pensioners / ex-MPs / freedom fighters / serving CGHS employees etc.: considered by the Additional Director of the CGHS city/zone, reimbursement restricted to CGHS package rates or actual expenditure, whichever is less.
  • (ii) Cases of procedural lapse (elective treatment in empanelled hospitals without Govt Specialist/CMO recommendation and without prior permission): considered by the Additional Director, same restriction (CGHS rates or actual, whichever is less).

Conditions (para 3)

  • The delegation does not cover cases involving relaxation of rules, irrespective of amount.
  • Cases above the limits go to MoHFW with IFD concurrence.
  • Reimbursement restricted to CGHS package / ceiling rate, or actual expenditure, whichever is less. Where no package or ceiling rate exists (para 2(B)), actual expenditure may be considered subject to admissibility, reasonableness and the limits.
  • All approvals subject to admissibility under CGHS rules, supporting records and bills, reasonableness of charges, budgetary provisions and audit requirements.
  • Powers are exercised case by case and create no general entitlement or precedent.
  • The revised delegations supersede earlier instructions to the extent of the financial delegations now conveyed.

Decentralised STC approvals (OM 01.09.2026)

CGHS OM F. No. 56-1/2026-27/CGHS/MSD (E-file 8392910) dated 01.09.2026 — decentralisation of approval procedure for selected STC-related cases.

Five categories decided by the Additional Director, CGHS within delegated financial powers
CategoryCases covered
1All transplant cases having notified CGHS package rates or guidelines
2Listed procedures, devices and treatment items with notified CGHS rates/guidelines — incl. TAVI, DBS, IVL, cochlear implants, CPAP, BiPAP, oxygen concentrators, CSII pumps
3STC-restricted medicines in the list displayed on the CGHS website
4Unlisted procedures, investigations, implants, medicines, devices and other treatments

  • No referral / permission / endorsement where treatment is at AIIMS, Institutions of National Importance, Tata Memorial Hospital or any other medical institution under the Central Government or a State Government [para 3(a)].
  • Approval (Categories 1–5) is accorded by the concerned Additional Director, CGHS within the delegated financial powers, if (i) supported by the recommendation / advice / prescription of one Government Specialist of the concerned specialty from such an institution, or (ii) failing that, by two specialists of the concerned specialty from two different CGHS-empanelled hospitals; (iii) every case is scrutinised by a three-member Local Technical Committee (headed by the AD with two GDMOs); (iv) for STC-restricted medicines the approved indication is verified against CDSCO approval / regulatory status.
  • Annexure I: cases outside the categories or above the AD’s delegated powers go to the Directorate. Deficiencies are ordinarily communicated within 3 working days; a complete case is ordinarily decided within 15 working days. Post-facto approval may be considered in an emergency / unavoidable circumstances / reasons beyond the beneficiary’s control, with recorded reasons — not an automatic entitlement. Records are kept for audit; monthly reports to the Directorate; mechanism reviewed monthly.

Dependent sons / brothers with critical / terminal illness

OM F. No. S.11030/54/2023-EHS(8248513)/I/3893459/2026 dated 01.09.2026 — relaxation in age and marital-status criteria for dependent sons and brothers suffering from critical / terminal illnesses under CGHS / CS(MA) Rules, 1944 (immediate effect).

  • Existing norms recited: unmarried dependent son — up to 25 years; permanently disabled unmarried son — for life; dependent brother — ordinarily up to 18 years, disabled dependent brother — no age limit; daughters and sisters (incl. divorced / abandoned / separated / widowed) already eligible.
  • New: CGHS / medical-attendance facilities may be extended for life to dependent sons and brothers suffering from critical / terminal illnesses, subject to the dependency conditions and assessment by the competent Medical Board.
  • Illnesses (indicative): chronic, severe, critical or terminal illnesses causing substantial and continuing functional impairment or inability to earn a livelihood / attain self-sufficiency — e.g. advanced malignancies, severe neurological disorders, end-stage organ disease, severe congenital / genetic disorders.
  • Eligibility is decided case by case (disease nature, functional impairment, ability to earn, continuing dependency); specialists assess multi-system conditions.
  • CGHS beneficiaries: assessed and recommended by decentralised Medical Boards at Additional-Director / Regional-HQ level; Appellate Medical Board at CGHS HQ for appeals. CS(MA) beneficiaries: assessed and recommended by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
  • Marital status: marriage is not a ground for cessation for a dependent son / brother covered on account of critical / terminal illness or permanent disability, provided dependency continues and the Board / authority recommends continuation. The relaxation does not expand “family” — it does not extend to his spouse or children.
  • Medical criteria are a “living framework”, reviewable by the designated CGHS Board.

Read from the published text of the OM.

OM F. No. S.11030/54/2023-EHS(8248513)/I/3909989/2026 dated 26.10.2026 — consideration of cases for dependent sons / brothers with critical / terminal illnesses under the decentralised STC mechanism.

  • Cases beyond the permissible age limit may be considered under the decentralised STC mechanism of Dte. of CGHS OM No. 56-1/2026-27/CGHS/MSD dated 01.09.2026.
  • As there is no standing Medical Board in CGHS, the advice / prescription of a Government Specialist of the concerned specialty is taken as the medical recommendation for examination by the Local Technical Committee (LTC) at the office of the Additional Director, CGHS; on its recommendation the card is issued / extended.
  • The card under this relaxation is issued initially for one year; extension beyond a year needs fresh medical / treatment records showing the continuing illness.

Exam note: the 01.09.2026 OM speaks of “decentralised Medical Boards”; the 26.10.2026 clarification says there is no standing Medical Board and the LTC procedure applies — the later OM governs the CGHS procedure.

Restricted drugs — GLP-1 (OM 24.07.2026)

OM No. 1-360/18-19/CGHS/MSD (2740767/P)-Part (1611)/EHS(8354138) dated 24.07.2026 — Injection Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) included in the Online List of Restricted Drugs under CGHS; Injection Tirzepatide and Injection Semaglutide are to be prescribed under CGHS and CS(MA) Rules only per Annexure-I (immediate effect).

  • Eligibility: BMI ≥ 35 kg/m², or BMI ≥ 32.5 kg/m² with one or more of: uncontrolled type-2 diabetes despite metformin + at least two other oral drugs; severe obstructive sleep apnoea; atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; MASLD; chronic kidney disease.
  • Contraindications: history of pancreatitis; personal / family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; pregnancy or lactation; severe NPDR or PDR; severe GERD, gastroparesis, inflammatory bowel disease or prior metabolic / bariatric surgery.
  • Prerequisites: treating specialist certifies lifestyle modification, dietary counselling and a supervised activity programme complied with for at least 3 months.
  • Prescriber: an Endocrinologist or Internal Medicine specialist of a Government hospital; every prescription endorsed by the concerned Head of Department; approval valid 6 months, continuation needs a fresh recommendation and endorsement.
  • Monitoring: monthly for the first 3 months, then every 3 months.

Billing guidelines — Annexure IV and vaccines

Annexure IV (Billing Guidelines) to CGHS OM 03.10.2025 — this is the current admissible / non-admissible billing guidance for empanelled hospitals:

  • Consumables: included in surgical package rates (no separate charge); in non-surgical cases with no package rate, reasonable use may be billed under consumables; vague entries such as “consumables kit” / “procedure kit” are disallowed.
  • Non-admissible (beneficiary pays): toiletries and personal-use items; cosmetics; non-medical services (telephone, TV, internet, attendant food, carry bags); attendant charges (ayah / ward boy, extra attendant bedding except the one bed in a private ward); mortuary / cremation charges; extra bedding beyond norm; the difference for implants / prostheses above what CGHS covers (only with prior consent).
  • Not to be billed separately at all (part of standard charges): glucometer strips, ECG electrodes, ventilator circuits / consumables, ward facilities (air / water / alpha bed, routine air-conditioning, infusion pumps, DVT pump, pulse oximeter / basic monitors, record photocopies), medical records / films / CD copies, vacutainers and syringes for investigations.
  • Table of common non-admissible items (21): home visit / consultation charges; bed pan; urine container / urobag; moisturizer; underpad, sanitary pad, bath wipes; room fresheners; hand sanitizers, mouthwash, depilatory creams, hand wash; spectacles / contact lenses after eye surgery; attendant food and mineral water; telephone / email / internet; mortuary sheet; protein supplements, sugar-free tablets, sweeteners; baby feeding bottles, formula, baby food; toiletries kit; baby set; barber / beauty services; welcome kit, carry bags; vaccinations not part of treatment; cosmetic procedures (e.g. LASIK for refractive error alone); tests or medicines irrelevant to the diagnosis on record; equipment repair / maintenance charges. Items 22–27 (e.g. attendant bed in a private ward, nurse administration of injections / infusions, tracheostomy care, NG feeding, IV cannulation) are included in ward / package / nursing charges.

The list is illustrative and covers analogous items.

Vaccines — official reply, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Q. 267 (02.12.2025): under extant CGHS guidelines vaccines are not admissible except Hepatitis B, influenza and Leprovac for high-risk individuals, on a specialist’s recommendation with justification, countersigned by the Head of Department of the concerned specialty of the Government hospital.

4 · Practice questions

Q1. Who has the power to authorise (appoint) private doctors as AMA?

The Head of Department (HoD) — by issuing an appointment order — but only when adequate Government doctors are not available within a 5 km radius (8 km by some references) and after he has verified the duly filled prescribed proforma and the doctor’s character and antecedents through the local police [Rule 2(a) GD(1)–(2)]. The appointment is subject to annual re-verification. Note: Rule 2(a)(A) itself lists the authorities that appoint Medical Officers (Dept of Health, other Depts of GoI, authorities declared Head of Department under SR 2(10), Chairman of the CGEWCC). The guide gives no OM number for the HoD’s power — see Verify tab.

Section: open

Q2. Who appoints the AMA under Rule 2(a)(A)?

(i) Department of Health, GoI (for persons in that Department) · (ii) any other Department of GoI (for its own persons) · (iii) any authority declared by the President under sub-rule (10) of Rule 2 of the Supplementary Rules to be the Head of a Department · (iv) the Chairman of the Central Government Employees Welfare Co-ordination Committee at stations where such Committees function.

Section: open

Q3. Can an honorary medical officer be an AMA?

No. Honorary Medical Officers outside hospital precincts are like private practitioners and are not AMAs (Note 5). Exception: in Andhra States they have been declared AMAs.

Section: open

Q4. Who can empanel / recognise a private hospital under CS(MA)?

MoHFW. Only private hospitals in non-CGHS-covered cities are considered; in CGHS cities the CGHS-empanelled hospitals serve the purpose. Separate guidelines exist for dental and eye hospitals.

Section: open

Q5. Who can permit an employee at a Government hospital to take indoor treatment in a private hospital?

The Head of Department, on the basis of the AMA’s medical prescription, for a hospital recognised under CGHS / CS(MA) [Rule 6 GD(3)].

Section: open

Q6. Up to what amount can a HoD settle a medical-reimbursement claim?

Up to Rs.10 lakh without IFD consultation, where no relaxation of rules is involved and entitlement is worked out strictly at prescribed CGHS / CS(MA) rates — OM File No. S.11030/4/2026-EHS(8385264) dated 16.02.2026 (earlier Rs.5 lakh by OM 23.11.2016, originally Rs.2 lakh). It covers permission cases and post-facto approvals. Above Rs.10 lakh: Ministry/Department with IFD consultation.

Section: open

Q7. What financial powers do CGHS authorities have for pensioners and other CGHS beneficiaries?

CGHS OM No. Z.15025/14/2/DIR/CGHS dated 25.06.2026: claims at approved rates — Additional Director, CGHS city/zone Rs.15 lakh (earlier 7), Director, CGHS Rs.25 lakh (earlier 15), Additional Secretary & DG, CGHS Rs.50 lakh (earlier 25); above Rs.50 lakh → MoHFW with IFD concurrence. Unlisted investigations / procedures / implants: AD Rs.2 lakh, Director Rs.5 lakh, AS&DG Rs.10 lakh; above → Ministry with IFD. Relaxation-of-rules cases are outside the delegation. Trap: the Rs.10 lakh figure belongs to HoDs of Ministries, not to the CGHS Additional Director.

Section: open

Q8. Who can grant permission or ex-post facto approval for treatment at a non-empanelled hospital?

The Additional Director of the concerned CGHS city / zone (pensioners, ex-MPs, freedom fighters, serving CGHS employees etc.), with reimbursement restricted to CGHS package rates or actual expenditure, whichever is less. The same authority considers elective treatment in empanelled hospitals done without Government Specialist / CMO recommendation or prior permission (procedural lapse) [OM 25.06.2026].

Section: open

Q9. Who approves unlisted procedures, restricted medicines and similar STC-type cases now?

The concerned Additional Director, CGHS, within delegated powers, after scrutiny by a three-member Local Technical Committee, supported by one Government Specialist’s recommendation (or two specialists of two different empanelled hospitals). All earlier OMs requiring Standing Technical Committee examination stand superseded [OM 01.09.2026]. Emergencies still go through the emergency / NHA route in the referral section.

Section: open

Q10. Who decides emergency cases, and is there a monetary limit?

Head of Ministry/Dept/Office for serving employees and Head of the CGHS-covered city for pensioners — no financial limit, within prescribed rates. HoDs have been delegated the power to decide “emergency” cases [Rule 6 GD(4)].

Section: open

Q11. Who can reject a medical claim, and does he need MoHFW’s permission?

The Controlling Officer in the Ministry/Department can reject any claim not meeting genuineness and other requirements, without consulting MoHFW. Cases needing clarification, interpretation or relaxation are referred to MoHFW [Rule 3 GD(3), Rule 9].

Section: open

Q12. Where is the appeal against rejection, and in what time?

To the Central Government, within 45 days of receipt of the rejection order [Rule 3 GD(4)]. Trap: it is not “appeal to MoHFW”.

Section: open

Q13. Who has the power to relax the rules?

MoHFW — rule-relaxation cases are referred to it; HoDs can settle only cases where no relaxation is involved.

Section: open

Q14. Who recommends treatment abroad, and who can allow it without prior approval?

The Standing Committee recommends (application through the employee’s Ministry/Department; prior approval mandatory). The Central Government may authorise reimbursement where prior approval was not feasible [Rule 11(7)] and may add or delete treatments in the Rule 11(3) Table by Gazette notification [Rule 11(4)].

Section: open

Q15. Who issues the CGHS card and who sponsors the application?

The Additional Director (AD), CGHS of the city issues the card; the application is sponsored by the Head of Department / Head of Office of the employee.

Section: open

Q16. Who issues a CGHS specialist referral and for how long is it valid?

Any Medical Officer of a CGHS Wellness Centre: valid 3 months, up to 3 specialists and 6 consultations. No referral is needed at Government hospitals (AIIMS, INIs, NE institutions, Tata Memorial, Central Govt hospitals, CGHS WCs).

Section: open

Q17. Who settles Ayah (nursing) charges, artificial appliances and confinement permissions?

Ayah charges: Head of Office (delegated). Artificial appliances: Head of Department. Confinement at a private recognised hospital: HoD may permit [Rule 8].

Section: open

⚠️ VERIFIED CORRECTION — Rule 8 of CS(MA) Rules 1944

Statute text (verified against official CS(MA) Rules 1944 PDF / LegitQuest / official reproduction):

  • Rule 8(1) — Charges for services rendered in connection with but not included in medical attendance/treatment: determined by authorised medical attendant and paid by patient.
  • Rule 8(2) — If any question arises whether any service is included, it shall be referred to the Government; decision of Government is final.
  • That is all. There is no Rule 8(3), 8(4), 8(5), 8(6), 8(7), 8(8), 8(9), 8(10), 8(11), 8(12), 8(13), 8(14), 8(15), or 8(16) in the 1944 Rules. Only 8(1) and 8(2) exist in the statute.
  • The entitlements discussed below (dental, maternity, ambulance, physiotherapy, cancer, disabled dependent, IVF, hearing aids, etc.) are real Government Decisions / Office Memoranda made under Rule 8(2), not statutory sub-rules. Coaching guides invent the numbering for readability. This guide now labels them correctly.

Sources verified July 2026: Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944 (official PDF via nitrr.ac.in / legitquest); MoHFW / DoPT / DoE / DOPT official orders.

🏥 A. CGHS — Establishment, Legal Basis, Administration & Coverage
Para 1

CGHS: Establishment, Constitutional/Statutory Basis, Administration, Coverage

Established 1954 | Administered by MoHFW | DG-CGHS | 80 Cities | www.cghs.gov.in
🆕 updated with 2026 orders
🆕 UPDATE — Who can join CGHS — 5 km rule removed (OM 17.09.2026)

OM F. No. Z.16025/227/2026/CGHS-III/EHS(8421134) dated 17.09.2026 — eligibility of serving Central Government employees for CGHS (immediate effect). It refers to OM No. C.14012/02/2018/CGHS-III/DIR dated 06.04.2018, under which CGHS coverage of serving employees was restricted to those residing / working within a 5 km radius of a CGHS Wellness Centre.

  • The geographical (5 km) criterion is totally dispensed with.
  • One-time option: serving employees residing / posted outside the earlier geographical coverage or in a city not covered by CGHS, who are on CS(MA) Rules solely for that reason, may opt to become CGHS beneficiaries, subject to other eligibility conditions and payment of the prescribed CGHS contribution.
  • Mandatory CGHS: serving employees residing or posted within the CGHS-covered area, i.e. the limits of the district headquarters where a CGHS Wellness Centre is situated, are mandatorily covered under CGHS and cannot opt out in favour of CS(MA).
  • Conditions of the option: one-time, final and binding; applies to all dependants (no splitting between the two systems); the employee keeps paying the CGHS contribution irrespective of residence / posting; no simultaneous claims under CGHS and CS(MA); no TA/DA for treatment or medicine procurement under CGHS rules; an undertaking that benefits will not be availed under both systems (inadmissible benefits are recoverable).
  • Employees who do not opt continue under CS(MA) Rules, 1944. False, incorrect or suppressed information attracts disciplinary action under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and recovery.

Effect on the exam answer: “CS(MA) applies where CGHS does not” is now only the default. A serving employee outside a CGHS area may choose CGHS once, irrevocably, for the whole family.

Read from the published text of the OM.

📜 Para 1.1 — Establishment & Nature
  • Full Name: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)
  • Established: 1954 — replaced the Contributory Health Service Scheme (CHSS)
  • Nature: A comprehensive health scheme — not an insurance policy — providing direct medical services + reimbursement to Central Govt employees, pensioners, and eligible dependents
  • Authority: Operated under the executive authority of the Government of India; no separate statute — governed by guidelines, OMs, and circulars issued by MoHFW
  • Administered by: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India
  • Directorate: Directorate General of CGHS (DG-CGHS) — headed by Director General (DG)
  • Field units: Additional Director (AD) offices in each CGHS city; Wellness Centres (WCs) at ground level

  • ABHA ID Linkage: Kept in Abeyance [OM 25.06.2024]
  • eSanjeevani tele-consultation
  • HMIS (C-DAC) Implementation [22.04.2025]
  • BCA portal (claims)

🔑 Key CGHS Principle

CGHS is NOT insurance. It is a service delivery + reimbursement scheme. Beneficiary contributes monthly — gets medical care from WCs and empanelled hospitals at CGHS rates — cashless or reimbursement basis.

⚠️ Exam Traps — Para A
  • "CGHS established in 1947 or 1960" — WRONG! 1954
  • "CGHS administered by Ministry of Finance" — WRONG! MoHFW
  • "CGHS card valid only at registered WC" — WRONG! Valid at any CGHS WC across India
  • "CGHS covers only allopathy" — WRONG! 6 medical systems
  • "WC opens at 9 AM" — WRONG! 7:30 AM
  • "CGHS is a statutory scheme with its own Act" — WRONG! No separate statute — governed by executive instructions and OMs
👥 B. CGHS Beneficiary Categories — All 13 Primary Categories
Para 2

13 Primary Beneficiary Categories under CGHS

CGHS Guidelines | MoHFW OM No. S.11012/1/2024-EHS dated 27.06.2024 (Card Guidelines) | CGHS Manual 2024
🔴 Critical
📜 Para 2.1 — 13 Primary Beneficiary Categories
  1. Employees drawing salary from the Central Civil Estimates (i.e., all Central Govt employees — IAS, IPS, IFS, Central Group A/B/C/D, etc.) and their eligible dependent family members — residing in a CGHS-covered area
  2. Retired Central Government pensioners drawing pension from Central Civil Estimates — and their eligible dependent family members
  3. Members of Parliament — both sitting and retired MPs
  4. Former Vice Presidents of India
  5. Former Governors and Lieutenant Governors
  6. Current or retired Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts
  7. Freedom Fighters
  8. Journalists accredited with the Press Information Bureau (PIB)
  9. Employees of the Railway Board (Note: Railway employees generally have separate Railway Health Facilities — but Railway Board employees in Delhi are covered under CGHS)
  10. Delhi Police personnel
  11. Employees of the Post and Telegraph Department
  12. Family pensioners on death of primary beneficiary (drawing family pension from Central Civil Estimates)
  13. Employees and pensioners of notified Autonomous/Statutory Bodies as extended by GoI from time to time

Additional categories extended: CISF personnel + CAPF personnel posted in CGHS cities; Supreme Court Legal Services Committee employees; Retired Air India employees with valid CGHS cards (bills through UTI ITSL portal) [OM Aug 2024]; DANICS and AGMUT cadre pensioners at par with AIS pensioners [OM 09.01.2026]; PSU Absorbees (from Govt to PSU) on fulfilment of conditions.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 C. Definition of Family & Eligible Dependents under CGHS
Para 3

Complete Definition of "Family" for CGHS — All Members, Age Limits, Income Conditions & Provisos

MoHFW OM No. S.11012/1/2024-EHS dated 27.06.2024 | OM H.11020/2/2023-EHS dated 26.07.2023 | OM S.14025/15/2024-EHS dated 28.03.2024 | CS(MA) Amendment 16.09.2025
🆕 updated with 2026 orders
📊 Visual summary — diagrams & comparison
🆕 UPDATE — Family: critical / terminal illness (OM 01.09.2026)

OM F. No. S.11030/54/2023-EHS(8248513)/I/3893459/2026 dated 01.09.2026 — relaxation in age and marital-status criteria for dependent sons and brothers suffering from critical / terminal illnesses under CGHS / CS(MA) Rules, 1944 (immediate effect).

  • Existing norms recited: unmarried dependent son — up to 25 years; permanently disabled unmarried son — for life; dependent brother — ordinarily up to 18 years, disabled dependent brother — no age limit; daughters and sisters (incl. divorced / abandoned / separated / widowed) already eligible.
  • New: CGHS / medical-attendance facilities may be extended for life to dependent sons and brothers suffering from critical / terminal illnesses, subject to the dependency conditions and assessment by the competent Medical Board.
  • Illnesses (indicative): chronic, severe, critical or terminal illnesses causing substantial and continuing functional impairment or inability to earn a livelihood / attain self-sufficiency — e.g. advanced malignancies, severe neurological disorders, end-stage organ disease, severe congenital / genetic disorders.
  • Eligibility is decided case by case (disease nature, functional impairment, ability to earn, continuing dependency); specialists assess multi-system conditions.
  • CGHS beneficiaries: assessed and recommended by decentralised Medical Boards at Additional-Director / Regional-HQ level; Appellate Medical Board at CGHS HQ for appeals. CS(MA) beneficiaries: assessed and recommended by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
  • Marital status: marriage is not a ground for cessation for a dependent son / brother covered on account of critical / terminal illness or permanent disability, provided dependency continues and the Board / authority recommends continuation. The relaxation does not expand “family” — it does not extend to his spouse or children.
  • Medical criteria are a “living framework”, reviewable by the designated CGHS Board.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — Beyond-age cases & LTC procedure (OM 26.10.2026)

OM F. No. S.11030/54/2023-EHS(8248513)/I/3909989/2026 dated 26.10.2026 — consideration of cases for dependent sons / brothers with critical / terminal illnesses under the decentralised STC mechanism.

  • Cases beyond the permissible age limit may be considered under the decentralised STC mechanism of Dte. of CGHS OM No. 56-1/2026-27/CGHS/MSD dated 01.09.2026.
  • As there is no standing Medical Board in CGHS, the advice / prescription of a Government Specialist of the concerned specialty is taken as the medical recommendation for examination by the Local Technical Committee (LTC) at the office of the Additional Director, CGHS; on its recommendation the card is issued / extended.
  • The card under this relaxation is issued initially for one year; extension beyond a year needs fresh medical / treatment records showing the continuing illness.

Exam note: the 01.09.2026 OM speaks of “decentralised Medical Boards”; the 26.10.2026 clarification says there is no standing Medical Board and the LTC procedure applies — the later OM governs the CGHS procedure.

Annexure-A — indicative list of 42 critical and terminal diseases
  1. Major organ / bone-marrow transplant (requiring, or post-transplant)
  2. All malignant tumours (solid and haematological)
  3. Congenital heart disease
  4. Eisenmenger syndrome
  5. Post CIED (PCD/CRT-D) with heart failure (EF < 35%)
  6. Symptomatic, haemodynamically significant valvular heart disease
  7. Severe left ventricular dysfunction, EF < 35%
  8. Cardiomyopathy
  9. Primary pulmonary artery hypertension
  10. Aortic aneurysm / dissections (treated or untreated)
  11. Demyelinating disease
  12. Degenerative / progressive nervous-system disorders
  13. Wilson’s disease (congenital metabolic and storage disorders)
  14. Refractory epilepsy syndromes
  15. Myasthenia gravis
  16. Autoimmune disorders
  17. Immunodeficiency syndromes
  18. Chronic liver disease
  19. Chronic pancreatitis
  20. Chronic bleeding disorders
  21. Congenital haemolytic anaemias
  22. Thrombotic microangiopathy – haemolytic uraemic syndrome
  23. Budd-Chiari syndrome
  24. Adrenal cancer / functioning adrenal tumours
  25. Diabetes mellitus type 1
  26. Endogenous Cushing’s syndrome
  27. Panhypopituitarism
  28. Chronic primary adrenal insufficiency
  29. Chronic respiratory failure
  30. Obstructive sleep apnoea requiring CPAP
  31. Severe bronchial asthma
  32. Chronic kidney disease
  33. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
  34. Congenital / hereditary progressive kidney disorders
  35. Bladder dysfunction (congenital / acquired) requiring continued intervention
  36. Major congenital genitourinary abnormality with residual functional defects
  37. Anatomic disorders of sexual dysfunction
  38. Moderate to severe psoriasis, PASI > 10
  39. Severe atopic dermatitis
  40. Severe pemphigus vulgaris
  41. Severe chronic urticaria
  42. Vitiligo > 10 to < 50% BSA

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — Family pensioners: divorced / widowed daughters (OM 28.10.2026)

OM File No. S.11030/321/2026-EHS(8430063)/I/3910699/2026 dated 28.10.2026 — inclusion and reinstatement of eligible divorced and widowed daughters in CGHS cards of family pensioners.

  • OM No. 37-1-97-C&P/CGHS/pt.III/CGHS(P) dated 26.05.1999 governs family-member eligibility; the guidelines had no provision to add or reinstate dependants in a family pensioner’s card after the primary cardholder’s death.
  • Now permitted: addition and reinstatement of eligible divorced or widowed daughters in the CGHS cards held by family pensioners, subject to verification of marital status, dependency, income and the other prescribed eligibility conditions. All other CGHS terms continue.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — Dependency income limit — DA now 63% (DoE OM 29.10.2026)

Department of Expenditure OM No. 1/2(i)/2026-E.II(B) dated 29.10.2026: DA enhanced from 60% to 63% of basic pay w.e.f. 01.07.2026. The CGHS dependency ceiling “Rs.9,000 + DA/DR” therefore works out to Rs.9,000 + 63% = ≈ Rs.14,670 per month (recompute at each revision).

🔴 Critical — Every Sub-Clause Has Exam Questions
📜 Para 3.1 — Complete "Family" Definition for CGHS (as per OM 27.06.2024)

Para 3.1(i) — Spouse:

  • Husband or wife (first wife only in case of adoptive father having more than one wife)
  • No dependency condition for spouse — spouse is automatically covered irrespective of income or employment status
  • If both husband and wife are Central Govt employees: both can have CGHS cards; only higher salary spouse makes the CGHS contribution

Para 3.1(ii) — Choice: Parents OR Parents-in-Law [MAJOR AMENDMENT — See Section D for full details]:

  • An employee has a choice to include EITHER dependent parents OR dependent parents-in-law — not both simultaneously
  • Both male and female employees can exercise this choice [OM 26.07.2023]
  • Subject to: (a) Dependency condition — income < Rs.9,000 + DA per month from all sources; (b) Normally residing with the Govt servant
  • Choice is a ONE-TIME OPTION — cannot be changed later [OM 13.05.2026]

Para 3.1(iii) — Children (including legally adopted, step-children, and wards):

  • Son: Till he starts earning OR attains the age of 25 years, whichever is earlier
  • Daughter: Till she starts earning OR gets married, whichever is earlier — irrespective of age limit
  • Son with permanent disability (physical or mental): Irrespective of age limit
  • Disability types covered: Blindness; Low vision; Leprosy cured; Hearing impairment; Locomotor disability; Mental retardation; Mental illness

Para 3.1(iv) — Dependent divorced/abandoned/separated from husband daughters AND widowed daughters:

  • Eligible irrespective of age limit
  • Also includes their dependent minor children (up to age of becoming major)

Para 3.1(v) — Dependent widowed/unmarried sisters:

  • Eligible irrespective of age limit
  • Dependent divorced/abandoned/separated sisters also included

Para 3.1(vi) — Dependent minor brother(s):

  • Up to the age of becoming a major (18 years)

Para 3.1(vii) [NEW — OM dated 16.09.2025] — Dependent Transgender children and siblings:

  • Dependent transgender children and siblings of Central Govt employees and pensioners — ANY AGE
  • Conditions: (a) Financially dependent AND (b) Valid certificate under Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019

📜 Para 3.3 — Key Rules on "Normally Residing"
  • Parents must "normally reside" with the Govt servant
  • Exception Exception: If a female Govt employee's parents/parents-in-law live in a different city — they can still be covered if other conditions met and residence condition is relaxed for female employees in specific cases [subject to OM provisions]
  • A Govt servant cannot claim medical reimbursement for his/her parents who are receiving Fixed Medical Allowance (FMA) — as FMA is a substitute for CGHS OPD benefits
  • If both husband and wife are Govt employees: they can claim for their respective parents (not combined) — each in their own card

Hinglish — Family Rules Yaad Karo
🗣️ Hinglish — Family Rules Yaad Karo
  • Spouse: Koi income condition nahi. Automatically covered.
  • Son: 25 saal tak ya kamana shuru kare — jo pehle. Permanently disabled → any age.
  • Daughter (normal): Jab tak unmarried hai — any age. Married → not eligible (UNLESS divorced/widowed/separated — then any age again).
  • Parents/Parents-in-law: Rs.9,000+DA se kam income. Aapke saath rehna chahiye. Ek ko choose karo — permanently.
  • FMA waale parents: NAHI milega — FMA = already getting OPD benefit substitute. Claim reject hoga.
  • 2-child rule: Medical reimbursement mein NAHI laagu. Kitne bhi bacche ho — sab covered.
⚠️ Exam Traps — Family Definition
  • "Married daughter cannot be CGHS dependent" — WRONG! Widowed/divorced/separated daughter = eligible at any age
  • "Parents-in-law eligible only if income < Rs.3,500" — WRONG! Current limit is Rs.9,000 + DA per month
  • "Both parents AND parents-in-law can be on CGHS card" — WRONG! Only ONE set — either parents OR parents-in-law
  • "Dependency condition applies to spouse" — WRONG! Spouse has no dependency condition
  • "2-child restriction applies for CGHS" — WRONG! NOT applicable
  • "Transgender dependents must be below 25" — WRONG! Any age with Transgender Persons Act 2019 certificate [16.09.2025]
  • "Suspended employee cannot claim for family" — WRONG! Suspended Govt servant entitled at par with working employee

🔴 Critical — Full Chronology + Current Position Under Latest OM 13.05.2026
📜 Para 4.1 — Legislative Chronology of Parents/Parents-in-Law under CGHS

Stage 1 — OM No. 4(1)-18/63-H dated 03.03.1987 (MoHFW):

  • Original provision: Only female Central Govt employees were given the choice to include either their parents or parents-in-law for CGHS benefits
  • Subject to: conditions of dependence and residence
  • Male employees: could only include their own parents (NOT parents-in-law)

Stage 2 — OM No. H.11020/2/2023-EHS dated 26.07.2023 (MoHFW):

  • MAJOR AMENDMENT: Both male and female Central Govt employees now have the choice to include either their parents OR parents-in-law
  • This OM superseded all earlier OMs on this subject for CGHS
  • Conditions: dependency (income < Rs.9,000+DA/month) AND normally residing with Govt servant
  • This change brought male employees at par with female employees

Stage 3 — OM No. S.14025/15/2024-EHS dated 28.03.2024 (MoHFW):

  • Extended the same facility to CS(MA) Rules 1944 beneficiaries at par with CGHS beneficiaries
  • So employees in non-CGHS areas (covered under CS(MA) Rules) also got this benefit

Stage 4 — OM No. S.14025/15/2024-EHS(8270534)/I/3862000/2026 dated 13.05.2026 (MoHFW):

  • KEY CLARIFICATION — ONE-TIME OPTION: A male Govt employee shall be eligible to exercise a one-time option ONLY for choosing either parents or parents-in-law
  • Once opted for parents → CANNOT switch to parents-in-law at any later stage — including in cases arising due to demise of parents or otherwise
  • Once opted for parents-in-law → CANNOT switch back to parents at any later stage
  • Applicable to BOTH CGHS and CS(MA) Rules, 1944 beneficiaries
  • All Ministries/Depts directed to circulate for strict compliance

📜 Para 4.2 — Conditions for Including Parents/Parents-in-Law (Current Position)

Conditions that MUST be met:

  • Condition 1 — Income: Monthly income of parents/parents-in-law from ALL sources (salary, pension, family pension, interest, rent, business, any other source) must be < Rs.9,000 + DA per month
  • Condition 2 — Residence: Parents/parents-in-law must normally reside with the Govt servant
  • Condition 3 — Not receiving FMA: If parents/parents-in-law are themselves receiving Fixed Medical Allowance (FMA) from their own pensionary benefits, they CANNOT simultaneously be covered under CGHS of their son/daughter (FMA = substitute for OPD benefits)
  • Condition 4 — One-time choice: Choice between parents OR parents-in-law is PERMANENT and one-time [OM 13.05.2026]
  • Condition 5 — Dependency declaration: Dependency declaration to be submitted to department/office sponsoring the CGHS card

Documents to be submitted:

  • Affidavit/Declaration of dependency (from Govt servant)
  • Income proof of parents/parents-in-law (pension slips, bank statements, etc.)
  • Proof of joint residence (ration card, electricity bill, etc.)
  • ID proof of parents/parents-in-law

🔄 Current Position After All Amendments (as on July 2026)
  • Both male and female CG employees: May choose EITHER own parents OR parents-in-law — NOT both [OM 26.07.2023]
  • Choice is ONE-TIME and PERMANENT — irrevocable even if chosen parents die [OM 13.05.2026]
  • Applicable to both CGHS and CS(MA) Rules beneficiaries [OM 28.03.2024 + OM 13.05.2026]
  • Income condition: <Rs.9,000+DA/month from all sources
  • Residence condition: normally residing with Govt servant
Hinglish — Parents vs Parents-in-Law
🗣️ Hinglish — Parents vs Parents-in-Law
  • Pehle (before 2023): Sirf female employees apne parents ya sas-sasur mein se ek choose kar sakti thin. Male employees sirf apne parents add kar sakte the.
  • 2023 OM: Ab male employees bhi choose kar sakte hain — apne parents ya sas-sasur — CGHS ke liye.
  • 2024 OM: CS(MA) wale employees ko bhi yahi facility mili.
  • 2026 OM (13.05.2026): Yeh choice SIRF EK BAAR hogi. Ek baar jo choose kiya — life bhar ke liye final. Parents choose kar liye → sas-sasur kabhi nahi aayenge (even if parents expire). Sas-sasur choose kar liye → parents kabhi nahi aayenge.
  • Income condition: Rs.9,000 + DA se kam income per month — all sources milake.
  • Rehna zaroori hai: Normally aapke saath rehte hone chahiye.
  • FMA waale parents: Agar unhe FMA mil raha hai — CGHS mein add nahi kar sakte (double benefit).
⚠️ Exam Traps — Parents vs Parents-in-Law
  • "Male employees can include parents-in-law only in 2024 onwards" — WRONG! Extension was in July 2023 for CGHS
  • "Employee can change from parents to parents-in-law if parents die" — WRONG! IRREVOCABLE even if parents die [OM 13.05.2026]
  • "Both sets of parents (own + in-law) can be included" — WRONG! Only ONE set
  • "Both husband and wife can claim for same parents" — depends — if both are CG employees, each can claim for their own respective parents
  • "CS(MA) employees don't get this parents-in-law benefit" — WRONG! Extended to CS(MA) in March 2024
  • "Option can be changed after 5 years" — WRONG! Lifetime decision — one-time only

🆕 UPDATE — Pensioner card via Bhavishya portal (OM 17.07.2026)

OM F. No. S.11012/1/2024-EHS(8283407)/I/3881628/2026 dated 17.07.2026 — CGHS web portal integrated with the Bhavishya portal for retiring employees (an additional mode; the existing online application on the CGHS portal continues).

  • Approved pension details on Bhavishya pre-fill the CGHS Pensioner Card application; PAN is the unique identifier for real-time validation.
  • After the Head of Office verifies the pension forms, the PPO is generated and the prescribed CGHS contribution is paid online through BharatKosh, the Pensioner Card is generated and can be downloaded from the CGHS Portal and the Bhavishya Portal.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — DANICS / AGMUT pensioners’ option (OM 09.01.2026)

OM File No. S.11030/147/2025-EHS(8366647)/I/3830861/2026 dated 09.01.2026 — Central Civil Service pensioners under DANICS and similarly placed AGMUT cadre employees may opt for medical facilities either from the State Government from which they retired or under CGHS, at par with AIS pensioners (OM No. S.11011/1/87-CGHS D.I/CGHS(P) dated 01.02.1988), on the same terms.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — Card issue where contribution is deducted (MoHFW OM 15.06.2004, as reproduced 2025)

MoHFW OM F. No. S-6252/2003-2004-R&H/CGHS/CGHS(P) dated 15.06.2004 (reproduced in CPWD OM 07.04.2025): CGHS is compulsory for Central Government employees whose recorded residence is in an area covered by a CGHS dispensary; benefits accrue from the date the employee applies for a CGHS card, but where the office is regularly deducting the CGHS contribution it is the office’s responsibility to ensure a card is issued, and the benefit cannot be denied merely because the employee did not apply; employees who do not apply despite written intimation are to be reported to senior officers.

Read from the CPWD OM reproducing the 2004 OM — relayed text. See also OM 17.09.2026 on mandatory coverage.

📜 Para 5.1 — CGHS Card: Physical Description & Colour Codes

The CGHS card is a white photo-ID plastic card with a coloured stripe at the top. The stripe colour indicates the status of the cardholder:

Stripe ColourCategory of Beneficiary
🔵 BLUEServing Central Government Employees
🟢 GREENPensioners | Ex-MPs | Retired Personnel | Freedom Fighters | Family Pensioners
🔴 REDSitting Members of Parliament
🟡 YELLOWPIB-accredited Journalists | Employees of Autonomous Companies

The card contains: Unique Beneficiary ID Number (BID); Name; Photograph; Dependent family members listed; Wellness Centre assigned; Pay Level/Entitlement; Validity date.

📜 Para 5.2 — Application Process for Serving Employees [OM 27.06.2024]
  • Step 1: Mandatory online application at www.cghs.nic.in → generate temporary reference number
  • Step 2: Fill the form online; take printout; affix photographs
  • Step 3: Submit hard copy to the concerned Department/Office (sponsoring authority = HoO/HoD)
  • Step 4: Department processes and submits to concerned Additional Director (AD), CGHS of the city
  • Step 5: AD office issues CGHS card
  • Requisition shall be sponsored by the Head of Department/Head of Office of the employee

📜 Para 5.6 — Card Fees, Replacement & Other Rules
  • New plastic card upon mutilation/renewal/loss: Form AA or BB + Bharatkosh Payment challan of Rs.100/-
  • Digital card: FREE
  • Card validity: Till primary beneficiary's retirement (serving employee); Lifetime if lifetime contribution paid (pensioner)
  • Card is not transferable from one employee to another
  • Loss of card: Report to police + CGHS authorities; duplicate card on FIR copy + application + fee
  • On retirement: Surrender blue card; apply for green (pensioner) card 6 months before retirement
  • Transfer to another city: Transfer online — no physical visit needed

Hinglish — Card Rules
🗣️ Hinglish — Card Rules

Colours: Blue = service mein; Green = pensioner/ex-MP/freedom fighter; Red = sitting MP; Yellow = PIB journalist/autonomous.

Digital card = plastic card: myCGHS app ya Digilocker mein CGHS card store karo — same validity. Free hai. Plastic Rs.100 lagta hai.

Pensioner ke teen options: (A) Full CGHS (OPD+IPD) — FMA nahi; (B) IPD-only card — FMA bhi lo; (C) Sirf FMA — koi card nahi. Ek baar choose karo — generally one-time.

⚠️ Exam Traps — Card
  • "Pensioner's card is Red" — WRONG! Pensioner = Green
  • "Sitting MP = Green card" — WRONG! Sitting MP = Red; retired MP = Green
  • "Digital card has less facility than plastic" — WRONG! At par with plastic card
  • "Digital card fee = Rs.50" — WRONG! FREE
  • "Plastic card replacement = Rs.50" — WRONG! Rs.100
  • "FMA pensioners cannot have any CGHS card" — WRONG! They can have IPD-only card

📜 Para 6.1 — Monthly CGHS Contribution (7th CPC, w.e.f. 01.01.2017)
Pay Level (7th CPC Pay Matrix)Monthly ContributionAnnual Contribution
Level 1 to Level 5Rs.250 per monthRs.3,000
Level 6Rs.450 per monthRs.5,400
Level 7 to Level 11Rs.650 per monthRs.7,800
Level 12 and aboveRs.1,000 per monthRs.12,000

Key rules:

  • Deducted automatically from monthly salary of serving employees
  • If both spouses are CG employees: Only ONE with higher salary contributes — single CGHS card covers the family
  • One subscription covers employee + ALL eligible dependent family members
  • CGHS contribution qualifies for deduction under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act — maximum Rs.25,000 per financial year

📜 Para 6.2 — Pensioner Contribution: Annual OR Lifetime Option

Option 1 — Annual Subscription: Pay 12 months × applicable monthly rate each year

Option 2 — Lifetime Card: One-time payment = 120 months (10 years) × applicable monthly rate

Pay Level at RetirementMonthly RateLifetime Card Payment (120×)
Level 1 to 5Rs.250Rs.30,000/-
Level 6Rs.450Rs.54,000/-
Level 7 to 11Rs.650Rs.78,000/-
Level 12 and aboveRs.1,000Rs.1,20,000/-

Proviso Key Provisos:

  • Proviso Proviso 1: Pensioner's contribution = same amount as at time of retirement — does not increase if rates are revised after retirement
  • Proviso Proviso 2: Pensioners who have already obtained lifetime validity card by paying lump sum — NOT required to pay any additional amount on revision of contribution rates
  • Proviso Proviso 3: Entitlement of pensioners who have deposited lifetime contribution — will NOT be changed on rate revision
  • Proviso Proviso 4: Family pensioner (after death of employee): Same contribution as the deceased was paying at time of death

📜 Para 6.5 — Fixed Medical Allowance (FMA) [MoP OM 16.02.2022]
  • Revised FMA: From Rs.1,000 to Rs.3,000 per month w.e.f. 1st January 2022 [MoP OM No. 4/28/2021-P&PW(D) dated 16.02.2022]
  • FMA is for: Pensioners/family pensioners residing in non-CGHS covered areas — in lieu of OPD facility under CGHS
  • Proviso Proviso 1 (Mutual exclusivity): FMA and CGHS OPD facility are mutually exclusive — cannot avail both simultaneously
  • Proviso Proviso 2 (Automatic stoppage): If pensioner shifts from non-CGHS to CGHS area → FMA automatically stopped — even without formal application from pensioner. Banks required to make this provision in their system [DPPW OM 24.03.2022]
  • Proviso Proviso 3 (IPD Exception): Pensioners taking FMA can STILL opt for an 'IPD Only' CGHS card for cashless indoor treatment at empanelled hospitals — after paying applicable CGHS contribution
  • Proviso Proviso 4 (Switch procedure): Pensioner wanting to switch from FMA to CGHS OPD → Apply to pension-disbursing bank in Form-2 for discontinuation of FMA → Bank issues certificate in Form-3 within 3 working days → Apply to CGHS for card with OPD facility
  • Extension to UPS employees: Benefits of FMA extended to employees covered under Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) — DPPW OM dated 13.03.2026

Hinglish
🗣️ Hinglish

Contribution: L1-5: Rs.250; L6: Rs.450; L7-11: Rs.650; L12+: Rs.1,000. Salary se auto kaat. Ek payment — poori family covered. Zyada salary wala spouse contribute karta hai.

Lifetime card: 120 mahine ki payment ek baar. L1-5: Rs.30K; L6: Rs.54K; L7-11: Rs.78K; L12+: Rs.1.2L. Baad mein rate badhne par kuch extra nahi dena.

FMA: 2022 se Rs.3,000/month. Non-CGHS city mein rehne wale pensioners ko milta hai — OPD ke badले. CGHS city mein shift ho gaye → automatically band. FMA + CGHS OPD simultaneously nahi milta. Par FMA + CGHS IPD card = allowed.

⚠️ Exam Traps
  • "Level 7-11 contribution = Rs.750" — WRONG! Rs.650
  • "FMA = Rs.1,000/month" — WRONG! Rs.3,000/month w.e.f. 01.01.2022
  • "Lifetime card for L1-5 = Rs.60,000" — WRONG! Rs.30,000 (250 × 120)
  • "After rate revision, lifetime card holders pay extra" — WRONG! No additional payment
  • "Ward entitlement based on pension amount" — WRONG! Based on basic pay drawn
  • "Section 80C deduction for CGHS" — WRONG! Section 80D
  • "FMA pensioners cannot have any CGHS benefit" — WRONG! They can have IPD-only card
  • "Both spouses pay CGHS contribution" — WRONG! Only higher salary spouse contributes

🆕 UPDATE — Restricted drugs: Tirzepatide & Semaglutide (OM 24.07.2026)

OM No. 1-360/18-19/CGHS/MSD (2740767/P)-Part (1611)/EHS(8354138) dated 24.07.2026 — Injection Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) included in the Online List of Restricted Drugs under CGHS; Injection Tirzepatide and Injection Semaglutide are to be prescribed under CGHS and CS(MA) Rules only per Annexure-I (immediate effect).

  • Eligibility: BMI ≥ 35 kg/m², or BMI ≥ 32.5 kg/m² with one or more of: uncontrolled type-2 diabetes despite metformin + at least two other oral drugs; severe obstructive sleep apnoea; atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; MASLD; chronic kidney disease.
  • Contraindications: history of pancreatitis; personal / family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; pregnancy or lactation; severe NPDR or PDR; severe GERD, gastroparesis, inflammatory bowel disease or prior metabolic / bariatric surgery.
  • Prerequisites: treating specialist certifies lifestyle modification, dietary counselling and a supervised activity programme complied with for at least 3 months.
  • Prescriber: an Endocrinologist or Internal Medicine specialist of a Government hospital; every prescription endorsed by the concerned Head of Department; approval valid 6 months, continuation needs a fresh recommendation and endorsement.
  • Monitoring: monthly for the first 3 months, then every 3 months.

Read from the published text of the OM (Annexure-I read up to the monitoring paragraph).

OM F. No. Z.15025/117/2017/DIR/CGHS/EHS(3132722) dated 16.05.2025 (continuing OM of 15.01.2018) — issue of generic / branded medicines at Wellness Centres: (1) medicines prescribed by specialists are supplied by the available generic name; (2) if available under an alternative brand of the same composition, that brand is supplied; (3) if available in neither form, it is indented by the same brand name through the Authorised Local Chemist. Subject to admissibility instructions issued from time to time.

📜 Para 7.2 — CGHS Formulary & Medicine Rules
  • Medicines dispensed at WC: from CGHS Formulary (approved list of medicines)
  • Chronic diseases: Medicines issued for 3 months at a time by any CGHS doctor against valid specialist prescription
  • Beneficiary going abroad: Medicines issued up to 6 months — with permission of Additional Director; requires copy of valid prescription + CGHS card + proof of travel
  • Collection deadline: Indented medicines must be collected within maximum 15 days of indent date
  • All medicines (including ALC-supplied): issued throughout duty hours of WC
  • No registration required at WC for collecting indented medicines
  • Doorstep delivery of medicines: available through speed post in certain cases
  • Medicines from empanelled private hospital on discharge: covered for ongoing treatment

🆕 UPDATE — Decentralised approval of STC cases (OM 01.09.2026)

CGHS OM F. No. 56-1/2026-27/CGHS/MSD (E-file 8392910) dated 01.09.2026 — decentralisation of approval procedure for selected STC-related cases.

Five categories decided by the Additional Director, CGHS within delegated financial powers
CategoryCases covered
1All transplant cases having notified CGHS package rates or guidelines
2Listed procedures, devices and treatment items with notified CGHS rates/guidelines — incl. TAVI, DBS, IVL, cochlear implants, CPAP, BiPAP, oxygen concentrators, CSII pumps
3STC-restricted medicines in the list displayed on the CGHS website
4Unlisted procedures, investigations, implants, medicines, devices and other treatments
5Robotic surgery for cancer cases
  • No referral / permission / endorsement where treatment is at AIIMS, Institutions of National Importance, Tata Memorial Hospital or any other medical institution under the Central Government or a State Government [para 3(a)].
  • Approval (Categories 1–5) is accorded by the concerned Additional Director, CGHS within the delegated financial powers, if (i) supported by the recommendation / advice / prescription of one Government Specialist of the concerned specialty from such an institution, or (ii) failing that, by two specialists of the concerned specialty from two different CGHS-empanelled hospitals; (iii) every case is scrutinised by a three-member Local Technical Committee (headed by the AD with two GDMOs); (iv) for STC-restricted medicines the approved indication is verified against CDSCO approval / regulatory status.
  • Annexure I: cases outside the categories or above the AD’s delegated powers go to the Directorate. Deficiencies are ordinarily communicated within 3 working days; a complete case is ordinarily decided within 15 working days. Post-facto approval may be considered in an emergency / unavoidable circumstances / reasons beyond the beneficiary’s control, with recorded reasons — not an automatic entitlement. Records are kept for audit; monthly reports to the Directorate; mechanism reviewed monthly.
  • Para 5: all existing OMs requiring Standing Technical Committee examination stand superseded and subsumed by this OM from the date of issue.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🔴 Critical — Every Clause & Sub-Clause Examinable
📜 Para 8.1 — Clause A: Government Hospitals — ZERO Referral Required

"Government hospital" [per OM Z.15025/18/2020 dated 09.10.2020 and re-iterated in OM 28.06.2024] includes:

  • All AIIMSs (All India Institute of Medical Sciences — New Delhi and all new AIIMS)
  • All Institutions of National Importance (INIs)
  • All North East Institutions
  • Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai
  • All other medical institutions under the Central Government
  • All Central Govt hospitals; CGHS WCs themselves

Provision: No referral/permission/endorsement shall be required for undergoing consultation, investigation, treatment procedure — including unlisted investigations/procedures — at any Government hospital.

Explanation Explanation: A CGHS beneficiary can walk directly into AIIMS or any INI for any treatment — no CGHS WC referral needed. Even if the procedure is not in the standard CGHS list (unlisted), it can be undertaken at Govt hospitals without endorsement.

📜 Para 8.2 — Clause B: Treatment at Private Empanelled Hospitals

Sub-Clause B(i) — Primary Referral for Specialist Consultation:

  • Referral issued by any Medical Officer of a CGHS Wellness Centre
  • Validity: 3 months from date of issue
  • During 3 months: Beneficiary may consult up to total of 3 specialists (the primary specialist + up to 2 more from different fields if recommended by primary specialist)
  • Maximum 6 consultations allowed within 3-month period (including repeat consultations with same specialist for acute illness)
  • Applies ONLY to referrals issued by CGHS MOs — NOT to referrals from Govt hospital specialists
  • HCOs must retain a scanned self-attested copy of the referral; return original to beneficiary
  • Portal: Quantity option for consultation = leave at default value of '1' — this does NOT mean only 1 consultation is valid; it is a portal instruction only

Sub-Clause B(ii) — Follow-Up at Same Hospital Only:

  • Subsequent follow-up consultations, investigations, or minor procedures: MUST be done at the same empanelled hospital where primary consultation was done
  • Not valid at another HCO — if beneficiary wants to go to a different hospital, a new referral is needed
  • Each follow-up visit on separate days: submitted as a separate claim on BCA portal

Sub-Clause B(iii) — Investigations and Procedures:

  • No further endorsement from CGHS required for routine listed investigations and minor procedures NOT requiring admission — within 3-month validity at same HCO
  • Exception EXCEPTION — CT Scan and MRI Scan: These are special investigations — require separate endorsement/referral from CGHS even within the 3-month validity period
  • If beneficiary wants tests done at a different Diagnostic/Imaging Centre (not the treating hospital): Tests prescribed by specialist of private empanelled HCO must be endorsed by CGHS Wellness Centre before proceeding [SOP OM 05.08.2024, Para 16]

📜 Para 8.5 — Clause E: Chronic/Special Conditions — Unlimited Follow-Up

Beneficiaries with the following 7 conditions may avail consultations and investigations without any time limit based on primary referral. No repeat referral/endorsement required:

  1. Post-cardiac surgery cases
  2. Post-organ transplant cases
  3. Post-neurosurgery cases
  4. End-stage renal disease (ESRD)
  5. Cancer treatment
  6. Autoimmune disorders
  7. Neurological disorders

⚠️ Exam Traps — Referral
  • "Referral valid for 6 months" — WRONG! 3 months
  • "Maximum 4 consultations per referral" — WRONG! Maximum 6 consultations
  • "Can visit any empanelled HCO for follow-up" — WRONG! Must be same hospital where primary consultation was done
  • "CT Scan needs no endorsement within 3-month validity" — WRONG! CT/MRI ALWAYS needs CGHS endorsement
  • "Emergency: AD approval needed for unlisted procedure" — WRONG! NHA portal — no AD approval
  • "Govt hospitals require referral for unlisted procedures" — WRONG! ZERO referral at Govt hospitals
  • "There are 5 chronic conditions" — WRONG! 7 conditions
  • "Quantity '1' in portal means 1 consultation only" — WRONG! Default '1' is a portal setting — does not limit consultations

🆕 UPDATE — OPD consultation Rs.700 / Rs.350 clarified (OM 13.01.2026)

OM File No. S.11030/168/2025-EHS(8378444) dated 13.01.2026 — clarification on OPD consultation charges under the revised CGHS rate list:

  • OPD consultation at Rs.700 is admissible only for consultations by Super Specialists (DM / MCh) in CGHS-empanelled hospitals, who hold a recognised DM/MCh qualification and consult in the concerned super-specialty discipline; the Rs.350 rate applies to other consultations.
  • For in-patient cases a maximum of two consultations per day per specialist is admissible, as per CGHS norms.
  • The CGHS Directorate OM of 24.03.2026 later reads “Super Specialist” in code CN003 as DM / MCh / DNB-SS or an equivalent qualification recognised by the National Medical Commission.

🔴 Critical — October 2025 is the MOST RECENT MAJOR AMENDMENT
🔄 Para 9.1 — Historic Rate Revision [DG-CGHS OM dated 03.10.2025, Effective 13.10.2025]

~2,000 medical procedures revised — first comprehensive revision since 2014. All existing MoAs with empanelled hospitals ceased from 13.10.2025 at 12 AM. HCOs must submit undertaking by 13.10.2025; sign fresh MoAs within 90 days.

📜 Para 9.2 — The 4-Dimensional Rate Framework (October 2025)

Dimension 1 — Hospital Accreditation:

  • NABH/NABL accredited hospitals: Standard Base Rate
  • Non-NABH/Non-NABL hospitals: 15% LOWER than NABH-accredited rate
  • Super-specialty hospitals (200+ beds): 15% HIGHER than NABH-accredited rate for corresponding super-specialties

Dimension 2 — City Tier Classification:

  • Tier I (X Cities): Standard Base Rate
  • Tier II (Y Cities): 10% LOWER than Tier I
  • Tier III (Z Cities): 20% LOWER than Tier I
  • Explanation Explanation: NE States (Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, etc.) + Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh → treated as Tier II (Y) rates

Dimension 3 — Ward Entitlement:

  • Semi-Private Ward: Base (Reference) Rate
  • General Ward: 5% LOWER than semi-private base rate
  • Private Ward: 5% HIGHER than semi-private base rate

Dimension 4 — Uniform Rate Items (NOT affected by ward entitlement):

  • Consultations (OPD/IPD)
  • Investigations/diagnostic tests
  • Radiotherapy
  • Day care procedures
  • Minor procedures not requiring admission
  • → These rates are UNIFORM across all wards

📜 Para 9.4 — CGHS Package Content (What is Included)

The CGHS package rate is an all-inclusive lump sum from admission to discharge covering:

  • Accommodation charges (including patient's diet)
  • Admission charges; Anaesthesia charges
  • Cost of medicines, consumables, disposables, surgical sundries
  • Doctor/consultant visit charges; Dressing charges
  • ICU/ICCU charges; Injection charges; Monitoring charges
  • Nursing care; O₂ charges; Ventilator charges
  • Operation charges; Operation Theatre charges
  • Physiotherapy charges; Procedural charges/Surgeon's fee
  • Registration charges; Related routine investigations during admission
  • Transfusion charges; Blood processing charges
  • Equipment charges (flowtron, infusion pump, syringe pump, etc.)

ProcedureReimbursement %
1st (Primary) Procedure100%

⚠️ Exam Traps — Package Rates
  • "Non-NABH gets 10% discount" — WRONG! 15% lower
  • "NE states = Tier III" — WRONG! NE + J&K + Ladakh = Tier II
  • "Consultations affected by ward type" — WRONG! Consultations/investigations are UNIFORM
  • "ICU = ICU charge + separate room rent" — WRONG! ICU Rs.5,400 is all-inclusive including accommodation
  • "2nd procedure in same session = 75%" — WRONG! 2nd procedure = 50%
  • "Cancer surgery rates revised in Oct 2025" — WRONG! Cancer surgery = old rates; only chemo/radio/investigations revised
  • "OPD consultation rate is Rs.150" — WRONG! Rs.350 [OM 12.04.2023]
  • "General ward room rent = Rs.1,000" — WRONG! Rs.1,500

🆕 UPDATE — Revised financial powers of CGHS authorities (OM 25.06.2026)

CGHS OM No. Z.15025/14/2/DIR/CGHS dated 25.06.2026 (Director, CGHS; IFD concurrence Dy. No. 1029 dated 18.06.2026) — “Revision of delegation of financial powers for settlement of medical reimbursement claims and grant of permissions/ex-post facto approvals in respect of pensioner CGHS beneficiaries and other eligible beneficiaries, including serving CGHS employees”. It revises the powers under the earlier OM No. Z.15025/79/2/DIR/CGHS dated 05.10.2016.

A. Medical reimbursement claims / hospital bills at approved rates — above Rs.50 lakh: MoHFW with IFD concurrence
AuthorityEarlier powerRevised power
Additional Director, CGHS City/ZoneRs.7 lakhRs.15 lakh
Director, CGHSRs.15 lakhRs.25 lakh
Additional Secretary & DG, CGHSRs.25 lakhRs.50 lakh
B. Unlisted investigations / procedures / implants (where no CGHS package or ceiling rate exists) — above Rs.10 lakh: Ministry with IFD concurrence
AuthorityEarlier powerRevised power
Additional Director, CGHS City/ZoneUp to Rs.1 lakhUp to Rs.2 lakh
Director, CGHSUp to Rs.3 lakhUp to Rs.5 lakh
Additional Secretary & DG, CGHSUp to Rs.5 lakhUp to Rs.10 lakh

C. Permissions / ex-post facto approvals

  • (i) Elective treatment / investigations in non-empanelled hospitals, diagnostic labs or imaging centres for pensioners / ex-MPs / freedom fighters / serving CGHS employees etc.: considered by the Additional Director of the CGHS city/zone, reimbursement restricted to CGHS package rates or actual expenditure, whichever is less.
  • (ii) Cases of procedural lapse (elective treatment in empanelled hospitals without Govt Specialist/CMO recommendation and without prior permission): considered by the Additional Director, same restriction (CGHS rates or actual, whichever is less).

Conditions (para 3)

  • The delegation does not cover cases involving relaxation of rules, irrespective of amount.
  • Cases above the limits go to MoHFW with IFD concurrence.
  • Reimbursement restricted to CGHS package / ceiling rate, or actual expenditure, whichever is less. Where no package or ceiling rate exists (para 2(B)), actual expenditure may be considered subject to admissibility, reasonableness and the limits.
  • All approvals subject to admissibility under CGHS rules, supporting records and bills, reasonableness of charges, budgetary provisions and audit requirements.
  • Powers are exercised case by case and create no general entitlement or precedent.
  • The revised delegations supersede earlier instructions to the extent of the financial delegations now conveyed.

🆕 UPDATE — HoD ceiling Rs.10 lakh — OM 16.02.2026 verified

Text of OM File No. S.11030/4/2026-EHS(8385264)/I/3840089/2026 dated 16.02.2026 verified: the ceiling for Heads of Departments of Ministries/Departments to settle medical-reimbursement cases (no relaxation of CGHS/CS(MA) Rules, entitlement strictly per prescribed rate lists) rises from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh without IFD consultation (earlier Rs.2 lakh → Rs.5 lakh by OM No. 11011/20/2014-CGHS(P)/EHS dated 23.11.2016); IFD concurrence CD No. 3131 dated 29.01.2026. This is the limit for HoDs of Ministries/Departments (serving employees under CGHS or CS(MA)); the CGHS administration’s own powers for pensioners and other beneficiaries are in OM 25.06.2026.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — CGHS final-claim time limit is 6 months (OM 01.06.2020) — replaces the 3-month rule

CGHS OM File No. 1-60/2017-CGHS/C&P/EHS (e-signed 01.06.2020) — “Revision of time limit for submission of final claims for reimbursement of medical expenses under CGHS”.

  • Earlier CGHS guidelines: 3 months. Revised to 6 months.
  • Only cases where bills are submitted after 6 months from the date of completion of treatment / discharge from hospital need to be taken up for condonation; the power of condonation and other terms are as in OM No. S.14025/8/99-MS dated 25.05.1999.

Correction made: the guide’s “CGHS = 3 months; CS(MA) = 6 months — different!” is obsolete. Both CGHS and CS(MA) final claims are now 6 months (CS(MA): 6 months from discharge / treatment; 1 month from discharge where an IPD advance was drawn). No later revision was found; confirm on the CGHS site before quoting.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — Medical advance where no package rate exists (OM 22.09.2021)

MoHFW OM No. Z.15025/8/2021/DIR/CGHS (signed 22.09.2021) — medical advance where no package rate is prescribed (refers to OM No. 14025/18/2015-MS/EHSS dated 17.10.2016: 90% advance for all treatment, OPD and IPD):

  • Admissible amount is computed item-wise at CGHS rates; for items with no CGHS rate, AIIMS rates; if there is none, the actual estimate.
  • The hospital seeking the advance must give an item-wise break-up of the estimate; 90% of the admissible amount so arrived at is advanced.
  • Other terms of the 17.10.2016 OM are unchanged.

CGHS OM F. No. Misc-29/25-26/H.Cell/CGHS(HQ)/EHS(8341458) dated 11.07.2025 — re-iterating OM No. 3749/2005/CGHS(P) dated 26.04.2006: the Secretary General of Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha can reimburse the medical claims of sitting MPs irrespective of monetary limits, even in relaxation of CGHS guidelines; such cases need not be referred to MoHFW or CGHS.

🆕 UPDATE — Who reimburses, tracking and grievance routes (Lok Sabha replies 2025–26)

Lok Sabha Unstarred Q. No. 1081 answered 24.07.2026 (MoHFW): reimbursement of claims of serving beneficiaries is done through their respective administrative Departments / Ministries; claims of pensioner beneficiaries are reimbursed by CGHS. Claims can be tracked on the CGHS web portal and the MyCGHS 2.0 app with the Claim ID generated at submission; dashboards in the CGHS HMIS module let Additional Directors and CMOs i/c monitor claims and processing days. Grievance routes: CGHS Grievance Portal, CPGRAMS, toll-free helpline / e-mail, complaint boxes at Wellness Centres, and the Local / Zonal Advisory Committees (LAC / ZAC).

Lok Sabha Unstarred Q. No. 1088 answered 25.07.2025: physiotherapy services can be availed at any public health facility or through CGHS-empanelled private HCOs; domiciliary physiotherapy is available as per OM No. S-11011/24/2011-CGHS(P) dated 01.06.2011.

Read from the Lok Sabha reply 1081 and the Lok Sabha reply 1088 — official parliamentary answers.

🔴 Critical — 3-Month CGHS vs 6-Month CS(MA); All Monetary Limits
📜 Para 10.1 — Medical Reimbursement Claims (MRC) — Complete Process
  • CGHS claim deadline: within 6 months of completion of treatment / discharge (OM 01.06.2020; earlier 3 months) — only claims after 6 months need condonation of delay (CS(MA) Rules also have a 6-month period)
  • Claim processing time: Average 21 days (60–120 days for non-empanelled hospital cases)
  • Submission portal: BCA (Beneficiary Claim Application) portal
  • SMS updates: Beneficiary receives SMS at every stage of MRC processing
  • Claim tracking: Via myCGHS app using claim number; CGHS website shows claims older than 1 month
  • OPD medicines claim: Can be submitted in the city of treatment — not necessarily home city [OM 08.05.2023]
  • Serving employees claim to: Respective Department/Ministry (NOT to CGHS office)
  • Pensioners claim to: AD (Additional Director) of CGHS city of registration
  • Cashless vs Reimbursement: At empanelled hospitals → cashless (direct settlement). Non-empanelled/emergency → pay first then claim reimbursement

🔄 Para 10.2 — Delegation of Powers [CGHS OM 16.02.2026, File No. S.11030/4/2026-EHS(8385264)]

Heads of Departments (HoDs) now have delegated powers to settle permission cases and post-facto approvals relating to Referral System and Medical Reimbursement under CGHS or CS(MA) Rules. ➕ Added — the actual substantive change: this OM enhances the ceiling for HoDs to settle medical reimbursement cases (no rule relaxation, entitlement per prescribed CGHS rates) from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh without needing IFD consultation — superseding OM No.11011/20/2014-CGHS(P)/EHS dated 23.11.2016 (which had earlier enhanced Rs.2 lakh → Rs.5 lakh).

📜 Para 10.4 — Medical Advance Rules
  • IPD Advance: 90% of approved CGHS package rates for all indoor treatments (irrespective of major or minor illness)
  • Requires certificate from treating Physician of Govt/recognized hospital
  • OPD Advance: Available if total estimated expenditure (tests/investigations) exceeds Rs.10,000 — advance = 90% of total estimate
  • Sanction timeline: Within 10 days of receipt of request
  • Ordinarily not more than one advance per same illness/injury
  • TB Advance: 80% of estimated cost OR Rs.36,000/-, whichever is less; applicable where treatment duration is more than 3 months
  • Medical advance recovered from balance of final claim after treatment
City Hinglish — Para 10.4 — Medical Advance Rules (Original → Hinglish, marker-by-marker)
🗣️ City Hinglish — Para 10.4 — Medical Advance Rules (Original → Hinglish, marker-by-marker)
