Original Para 10.4 — Medical Advance Rules: Yeh parent original text hai; iske neeche ke saare sub-points isi provision ke under read honge.
Hinglish: Medical advance ke rules. IPD advance: approved CGHS package rates ka 90% — saare indoor treatments ke liye (chhoti ya badi bimari, koi fark nahi). Zaroori: treating Physician (Govt/recognized hospital) ka certificate. OPD advance: tab jab total estimate Rs.10,000 se zyada ho — advance = estimate ka 90%. Sanction timeline: request milne ke 10 din ke andar. Ek hi bimari/chot ke liye aam taur par ek se zyada advance nahi. TB advance: estimated cost ka 80% YA Rs.36,000 — jo kam ho (jab ilaaj 3 months se lamba ho). Final claim settle hone ke baad advance balance se adjust/vasool hota hai.
Original IPD Advance: 90% of approved CGHS package rates for all indoor treatments (irrespective of major or minor illness)
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: 90% of manzoor CGHS package rates (dar) ke liye all indoor treatments (chahe kuch bhi ho — badi ya chhoti bimari) Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam.
Original Sub-point 2: Requires certificate from treating Physician of Govt/recognized hospital
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: Ki zaroorat hoti hai certificate (pramaan patra) se treating Physician of Govt/recognized (manyata prapt) hospital Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam.
Original OPD Advance: Available if total estimated expenditure (tests/investigations) exceeds Rs.10,000 — advance = 90% of total estimate
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: Upalabdh (available) agar total estimated kharcha (tests/investigations (jaanch/tests)) se zyada hai Rs.10,000 — advance (pehle se di gayi raashi) = 90% of total estimate Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam. Important figures/dates: Rs.10,000.
Worked Example: Worked example: Rs.20,000 estimate par 90% advance = Rs.18,000, subject to approval.
Original Sanction timeline: Within 10 days of receipt of request
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: Ke andar 10 days of receipt of request Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam. Important figures/dates: 10 days.
Original one advance: Ordinarily not more than one advance per same illness/injury
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: Ordinarily NAHI se zyada one advance (pehle se di gayi raashi) per same bimari/injury Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam.
Original TB Advance: 80% of estimated cost OR Rs.36,000/- , whichever is less; applicable where treatment duration is more than 3 months
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: 80% of estimated cost ya Rs.36,000/-, — jo bhi kam ho; laagu jahan ilaaj duration hai se zyada 3 months Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam. Important figures/dates: Rs.36,000/-, 3 months.
Worked Example: Worked example: TB estimate Rs.50,000 par 80% = Rs.40,000, lekin Rs.36,000 cap hone par admissible advance Rs.36,000 hoga.
Original Sub-point 7: Medical advance recovered from balance of final claim after treatment
Hinglish: Medical advance ka yeh rule: Medical advance (pehle se di gayi raashi) vasool kiya gaya se balance of final claim (daava) ke baad ilaaj Exam trap: IPD advance = 90% (80% nahi), OPD advance tabhi jab estimate > Rs.10,000, TB = 80% ya Rs.36,000 jo kam.
📜 Para 10.5 — Dual Insurance + CGHS Reimbursement
  • Beneficiaries subscribed to both Medical Insurance + CGHS may claim from both sources
  • Condition: Total reimbursement from both sources CANNOT exceed actual expenditure
  • Sequence: First claim on insurance company → insurance company certifies amount reimbursed → beneficiary then claims remaining from CGHS with duplicate bills (certified by insurer)
  • CGHS reimbursement restricted to admissible amount per CGHS rates

Original Para 10.5 — Dual Insurance + CGHS Reimbursement: Yeh parent original text hai; iske neeche ke saare sub-points isi provision ke under read honge.
Hinglish: Medical insurance + CGHS dono hone par kya hota hai. Beneficiary dono sources se claim kar sakta hai — par TOTAL reimbursement actual expenditure se zyada NAHI ho sakta (double benefit nahi milega). Sequence: pehle insurance company se claim karo → company certified amount de → phir bacha hua amount CGHS se duplicate bills (company ki certification ke saath) claim karo. CGHS ka reimbursement apni prescribed rates ke hisaab se hi hota hai — admissible amount tak.
Original Sub-point 1: Beneficiaries subscribed to both Medical Insurance + CGHS may claim from both sources
Hinglish: Dual insurance ka yeh rule: Beneficiaries (labharthi) subscribed se dono Medical insurance (bima) + CGHS sakta hai claim (daava) se dono sources Yaad rakho: insurance + CGHS = allowed, par total > actual kharcha NAHI; pehle insurance, phir CGHS (balance ke liye).
Original Condition: Total reimbursement from both sources CANNOT exceed actual expenditure
Hinglish: Dual insurance ka yeh rule: Total reimbursement (kharcha wapas milna) se dono sources NAHI sakta se zyada hona actual kharcha Yaad rakho: insurance + CGHS = allowed, par total > actual kharcha NAHI; pehle insurance, phir CGHS (balance ke liye).
Original Sequence: First claim on insurance company → insurance company certifies amount reimbursed → beneficiary then claims remaining from CGHS with duplicate bills (certified by insurer)
Hinglish: Dual insurance ka yeh rule: Pehla claim (daava) par insurance (bima) company → insurance (bima) company certify karta hai rakam kharcha wapas milta hai → beneficiary (labharthi) then claims (daave) remaining se CGHS with duplicate bills (bijak) (certify kiya hua dwara bima company) Yaad rakho: insurance + CGHS = allowed, par total > actual kharcha NAHI; pehle insurance, phir CGHS (balance ke liye).
Original Sub-point 4: CGHS reimbursement restricted to admissible amount per CGHS rates
Hinglish: Dual insurance ka yeh rule: CGHS reimbursement (kharcha wapas milna) seemit se admissible (manzoor) rakam per CGHS rates (dar) Yaad rakho: insurance + CGHS = allowed, par total > actual kharcha NAHI; pehle insurance, phir CGHS (balance ke liye).
⚠️ Exam Traps — Reimbursement
  • "CGHS claim must be within 3 months" — WRONG! 6 months since OM 01.06.2020 (CS(MA) is also 6 months)
  • "IPD advance = 80%" — WRONG! 90%
  • "TB advance = 90%" — WRONG! 80% or Rs.36,000 (whichever less)
  • "Advance within 30 days" — WRONG! 10 days
  • "OPD advance always available" — WRONG! Only if estimate > Rs.10,000
  • "Pensioners submit MRC to CGHS WC" — More precisely: to AD (Additional Director) office of CGHS city
  • "Serving employees submit MRC to CGHS office" — WRONG! To their own Department/Ministry

🆕 UPDATE — Cochlear implants — revised ceilings (OM 09.11.2026)

OM F. No. S-367/2026/CGHSHQ/R&H/EHS(8410942)/I/3913657/2026 dated 09.11.2026 (IFD concurrence CD No. 2680 dated 04.11.2026) — revised ceiling rates and guidelines for cochlear implantation and rehabilitation under CGHS and CS(MA) Rules, 1944. It refers to OM No. 6-469/2003-CGHS/R&H dated 12 June 2009 and supersedes earlier orders on cochlear implantation (existing sanctions continue on their terms).

Unilateral implantation — package cost or actual admissible expenditure, whichever is lower
CategoryPackage ceiling (incl. GST)
Pre-lingual deafnessRs.7,00,000
Post-lingual deafnessRs.6,00,000
  • Eligibility — pre-lingual: children 9 months to 7 years with severe-to-profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss; hearing-aid trial of 3–6 months without appreciable benefit (urgent surgery may be considered in meningitis / cochlear ossification); no intellectual disability, active middle-ear disease, cochlear aplasia, cochlear nerve agenesis, retrocochlear lesion or central deafness; any tympanic perforation closed ≥ 3 months earlier; adequate family support. Post-lingual: severe-to-profound bilateral sensorineural loss, any age, with chronic ear disease treated and retrocochlear / central disorders excluded.
  • Implant: multichannel, CDSCO-approved, admissible for all ages; surgery at Government hospitals, AIIMS, INIs, autonomous Government hospitals or CGHS-empanelled / CS(MA)-recognised hospitals with implant facilities and rehabilitation arrangements.
  • Advice: one ENT specialist of a Government institution (AIIMS, INI, Tata Memorial, any Central/State Government institution); otherwise two ENT specialists of two different CGHS-empanelled hospitals (para 3(b) of OM 01.09.2026).
  • Approval: prior approval is mandatory; for serving and pensioners the Additional Directors (zone/city) permit it under the decentralised STC OM 01.09.2026, Category 2. Initially unilateral; the other side after 1 year with justification and assessment. CGHS applications route through Wellness Centres to the AD; CS(MA) beneficiaries through their Ministry/Department/Office to DGHS.
  • Replacement: wear-and-tear upgradation of eligible wearable components after 3 years (excluding cords and batteries), reimbursement limited to 50% of package cost or actual, whichever is lower.

  • "Cochlear implant = Rs.3 lakh" — WRONG! Rs.7,00,000 (pre-lingual) / Rs.6,00,000 (post-lingual), incl. GST [OM 09.11.2026]

  • "IVF for any married woman" — WRONG! Only married woman CG servant aged 21–39 years

  • "Ambulance always reimbursed" — WRONG! Only with specific medical certificate

🚫 M. Non-Admissible Items under CGHS — Complete List
Para 13

Complete List of Non-Admissible Items — CGHS Guidelines + SOP OM 02.09.2024

CGHS Manual | SOP OM 02.09.2024 | CGHS Circular on Non-admissible items
🆕 updated with 2026 orders
🆕 UPDATE — Current billing guidelines — Annexure IV of OM 03.10.2025; vaccines

Annexure IV (Billing Guidelines) to CGHS OM 03.10.2025 — this is the current admissible / non-admissible billing guidance for empanelled hospitals:

  • Consumables: included in surgical package rates (no separate charge); in non-surgical cases with no package rate, reasonable use may be billed under consumables; vague entries such as “consumables kit” / “procedure kit” are disallowed.
  • Non-admissible (beneficiary pays): toiletries and personal-use items; cosmetics; non-medical services (telephone, TV, internet, attendant food, carry bags); attendant charges (ayah / ward boy, extra attendant bedding except the one bed in a private ward); mortuary / cremation charges; extra bedding beyond norm; the difference for implants / prostheses above what CGHS covers (only with prior consent).
  • Not to be billed separately at all (part of standard charges): glucometer strips, ECG electrodes, ventilator circuits / consumables, ward facilities (air / water / alpha bed, routine air-conditioning, infusion pumps, DVT pump, pulse oximeter / basic monitors, record photocopies), medical records / films / CD copies, vacutainers and syringes for investigations.
  • Table of common non-admissible items (21): home visit / consultation charges; bed pan; urine container / urobag; moisturizer; underpad, sanitary pad, bath wipes; room fresheners; hand sanitizers, mouthwash, depilatory creams, hand wash; spectacles / contact lenses after eye surgery; attendant food and mineral water; telephone / email / internet; mortuary sheet; protein supplements, sugar-free tablets, sweeteners; baby feeding bottles, formula, baby food; toiletries kit; baby set; barber / beauty services; welcome kit, carry bags; vaccinations not part of treatment; cosmetic procedures (e.g. LASIK for refractive error alone); tests or medicines irrelevant to the diagnosis on record; equipment repair / maintenance charges. Items 22–27 (e.g. attendant bed in a private ward, nurse administration of injections / infusions, tracheostomy care, NG feeding, IV cannulation) are included in ward / package / nursing charges.

The list is illustrative and covers analogous items.

Vaccines — official reply, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Q. 267 (02.12.2025): under extant CGHS guidelines vaccines are not admissible except Hepatitis B, influenza and Leprovac for high-risk individuals, on a specialist’s recommendation with justification, countersigned by the Head of Department of the concerned specialty of the Government hospital.

Read from the published text of Annexure IV and the Rajya Sabha reply.

🔴 Critical — Frequently Tested
📜 Para 13.1 — Non-Admissible Items
  • ❌ Treatment outside India (except under specific Standing Committee approval)
  • ❌ Routine injections/dressings administered at patient's residence
  • ❌ Treatment at non-empanelled private hospitals in non-emergency conditions — no claim entertained
  • ❌ Eyesight testing for family members (only employee, once in 3 years)
  • ❌ Spectacle frames and lenses at Govt expense
  • ❌ Orthodontic treatment (braces, aligners, retainers)
  • ❌ Cosmetic/aesthetic treatment or surgery for improving general physical fitness/figure/stamina
  • ❌ Tonics, food supplements, vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, milk powder, glucose/energy powders
  • ❌ Toilet preparations, cosmetics, disinfectants, antiseptics
  • ❌ Ayurvedic preparations prescribed by Allopathic doctors
  • ❌ Vaccines (in general) — not admissible as a general rule
  • ❌ Medicines recommended orally/telephonically by doctor (no written prescription)
  • ❌ Dietary supplements classified as food items
  • ❌ AICD (Automated Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator)
  • ❌ Patient convenience/hospitality items: Laundry charges; newspapers/TV; phone charges; food/beverages beyond prescribed diet
  • ❌ ECG electrodes/leads (included in ECG test rate)
  • ❌ Bedside glucose test strip charges (included in ICU/investigation charges)
  • ❌ CT/MRI scan film/CD copies (included in package rate)
  • ❌ Blood sugar test at bedside separately (included in bedside monitoring charges)
  • ❌ Items not directly related to treatment and primarily for patient convenience

🌟 N. AUTHORITATIVE Q&A — Parents-in-Law Reimbursement Eligibility (Verified by All Latest Orders)
Q&A

Parents-in-Law on CGHS Card: Are They Eligible for Medical Reimbursement from the Serving Employee's Office?

Verified by MoHFW, DoPPW, DoPT, DoE & GoI Orders
❓ Authentic Question | Verified by MoHFW, DoPPW, DoPT, DoE & GoI Orders | July 2026

Parents-in-Law on CGHS Card: Are They Eligible for Medical Reimbursement from the Serving Employee's Office?

❓ Question Asked

"I am working as a Central Government employee. I am a CGHS beneficiary along with my wife and parents-in-law. My doubt is: Me and my wife are eligible for reimbursement of amount spent after CGHS reference. What about my parents-in-law? They have a CGHS card and medicines are constantly issued from CGHS. Are they eligible for medical claim reimbursement from my office (they are my dependents)?"

✅ AUTHORITATIVE ANSWER — Short Answer

YES — Your parents-in-law ARE eligible for medical reimbursement from your office, subject to important conditions being met.

Since your parents-in-law are enrolled as dependents on your CGHS card, they are entitled to the same CGHS benefits as you — including cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals and medical reimbursement claims from your department/office.

✅ DETAILED ANSWER — Analysis as per All Latest Orders

POINT 1: LEGAL BASIS FOR INCLUDING PARENTS-IN-LAW

  • The facility of including parents-in-law in CGHS was originally available only to female Central Govt employees — vide MoHFW OM No. 4(1)-18/63-H dated 03.03.1987
  • This was significantly expanded by MoHFW OM No. H.11020/2/2023-EHS dated 26.07.2023 — now both male and female CG employees can choose either own parents OR parents-in-law
  • Further clarified by MoHFW OM No. S.14025/15/2024-EHS(8270534)/I/3862000/2026 dated 13.05.2026 — this option is a one-time, irreversible choice
  • Since you have already included your parents-in-law as dependents, they are legally recognized dependents under CGHS

POINT 2: CONDITIONS THAT MUST HAVE BEEN MET FOR THEIR INCLUSION

  • Income Condition: Their monthly income from ALL sources must be < Rs.9,000 + DA per month [MoHFW OM 27.06.2024 — Card Guidelines]. If their income exceeds this, they are NOT eligible dependents
  • Residence Condition: They must normally reside with you [OM 27.06.2024]
  • Choice Condition: You have exercised the option to include parents-in-law (not your own parents) — this is a one-time irrevocable choice [OM 13.05.2026]
  • FMA Condition: Your parents-in-law should NOT be receiving Fixed Medical Allowance (FMA) from their own pension/retirement benefits — FMA and CGHS coverage are mutually exclusive [CGHS guidelines]

POINT 3: REIMBURSEMENT ENTITLEMENT — WHAT IS ADMISSIBLE

  • Since parents-in-law are on your CGHS card as dependents → they are CGHS beneficiaries
  • OPD reimbursement: Medicines issued from CGHS WC are FREE (no reimbursement needed — directly issued). If they buy OPD medicines from outside after CGHS reference — claim within 6 months from your department
  • IPD reimbursement: If hospitalized at empanelled hospital with CGHS referral → cashless treatment. If paid out of pocket → claim reimbursement from your department within 6 months. Reimbursement at CGHS rates or actual — whichever is less
  • Investigation charges: Listed investigations after CGHS referral at empanelled hospital → reimbursable
  • Emergency treatment: Even at non-empanelled hospital → reimbursement at Non-NABH rates of concerned city or actual, whichever less
  • CGHS medicines already being issued: This confirms they are enrolled and benefiting — reimbursement for additional expenses follows the same CGHS rules

POINT 4: FROM WHICH OFFICE/DEPARTMENT TO CLAIM

  • Since you are a serving Central Govt employee — ALL medical reimbursement claims (for yourself, wife, AND parents-in-law) are submitted to your own Ministry/Department/Office — where you work
  • NOT to the CGHS AD office (that is for pensioners)
  • The claim is submitted to your Head of Office who forwards to the Bill Passing Authority
  • Reimbursement paid to you (the CGHS card primary holder) — not to parents-in-law separately

POINT 5: DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FOR PARENTS-IN-LAW MRC

  • Copy of valid CGHS card showing parents-in-law as dependents
  • CGHS referral/prescription (for OPD treatment at empanelled hospitals)
  • Original bills/prescriptions
  • Discharge summary (for IPD cases)
  • Emergency certificate (if emergency treatment)
  • Dependency declaration (already on file with department)
  • Claim submitted within 6 months of completion of treatment / discharge

POINT 6: CRITICAL CONDITION — ARE YOUR PARENTS-IN-LAW RECEIVING FMA?

  • If your parents-in-law (or your wife's parents) are retired Central Govt employees receiving FMA (Fixed Medical Allowance) from their own pension → they CANNOT simultaneously be enrolled on your CGHS card as dependents for OPD purposes
  • However: If they have an 'IPD only' CGHS card (using FMA for OPD) — their IPD treatment through your CGHS card for hospitalization is possible subject to conditions
  • If they are receiving another Ministry's/Autonomous Body's medical benefit → they generally cannot claim double benefits

⚠️ IMPORTANT CAVEATS — Read Carefully
  1. Income check is crucial: If parents-in-law earn more than Rs.9,000+DA/month, they should NOT have been enrolled. If this is discovered, past claims may be denied. Verify income compliance immediately.
  2. Residence check: If parents-in-law do not normally reside with you, their inclusion may be questioned. Keep documentary proof (joint ration card, electricity bills, etc.)
  3. Wife's department: Your wife CANNOT separately claim for the same parents-in-law from her office (unless they are her own parents — different cards). CGHS claim for a dependent goes through ONE primary card holder only.
  4. Both husband and wife as CG employees: Each can have their own CGHS card. If parents-in-law are on YOUR card, YOU claim. If they were on your WIFE's card, she claims. Cannot claim from both offices for same dependent.
  5. If parents-in-law received FMA: Their enrollment on your CGHS card for OPD purposes is not proper — only IPD coverage possible. Rectify this immediately with CGHS and your department.
  6. One-time option irrevocable [OM 13.05.2026]: Since you have included parents-in-law (exercising the option), you CANNOT switch to your own parents later — even if your parents-in-law pass away.
✅ SUMMARY ANSWER — 4 Key Points
  1. YES — Eligible: Parents-in-law on CGHS card as dependents are FULLY eligible for CGHS benefits including reimbursement of medical claims — if all conditions are met
  2. Claim from YOUR office: Submit medical reimbursement claim to your own Ministry/Department — not to CGHS AD office (that's for pensioners)
  3. Within 6 months: Submit claim within 6 months of completion of treatment / discharge (OM 01.06.2020)
  4. CGHS rates apply: Reimbursement at CGHS package rates or actual — whichever is less
👴 Q. Special Provisions for Senior Beneficiaries (70+ & 80+)
Senior Citizens

Special Facilities for Elderly — No Referral (70+), Home Visits (80+), Priority & Cashless access

OM 28.06.2024 (70+ Referral) | July 2017 (80+ Provisions) | AIIMS Cashless OMs 2023
🔴 Critical for Exam
📜 Q.1 — Provisions for Beneficiaries Aged 70 Years and Above
  • Referral-Free Consultation: Can consult any specialist at empanelled private hospitals without any referral from CGHS Wellness Centre.
  • Investigations: Can undergo any listed investigation/procedure prescribed by the specialist without further endorsement.
  • Unlisted Items: Still require prior approval from CGHS authorities.
  • Earlier Limit: This age limit was 75 years (fixed in 2019) — reduced to 70 years vide OM dated 28.06.2024.
📜 Q.2 — Special Provisions for Beneficiaries Aged 80 Years and Above
  • Queue-free: Consultation at CGHS Wellness Centres without standing in queue.
  • Home Visit: MO/CMO of Wellness Centre to make a home visit once a month if the beneficiary is unable to attend and resides within 5 KM of the Wellness Centre.
  • Phone enquiry: Doctors to enquire about wellbeing over phone at least once a month.
  • Priority Settlement: Medical reimbursement claims (MRCs) of 80+ beneficiaries settled on out-of-turn priority basis.
  • Physician continuity: Can continue follow-up treatment with the same specialist even in a non-empanelled hospital (due to age-related difficulty), with reimbursement limited to CGHS rates.
📜 Q.3 — Cashless access to Premium Government Institutes
  • CGHS Pensioners and other eligible categories (MPs, etc.) can avail cashless treatment at AIIMS (New Delhi + Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Raipur, Patna, Rishikesh, Jodhpur), PGIMER Chandigarh, JIPMER Puducherry, NEIGRIHMS Shillong & RIMS Imphal.
  • Bills are settled directly by CGHS with the institutes; no need for reimbursement filing by beneficiary.
Hinglish — Senior Citizen Rules

  • 80+ age: VIP treatment! Queue mein mat khade ho. 5 KM ke andar ho to doctor ghar aayega (home visit). Bill payment sabse pehle hogi (priority). Doctor phone par haal-chaal puchega.
  • AIIMS/PGI: Cashless facility — bill ki chinta nahi, Govt degi.

⚖️ A. Preamble & Constitutional Basis of CS(MA) Rules, 1944
Preamble

Constitutional/Statutory Basis, Nature, Scope & Relationship with CGHS

Government of India Act, 1935 S.241(2) read with S.313(3) | Notified: 1st January 1944
🆕 updated with 2026 orders
🆕 UPDATE — CS(MA) vs CGHS — one-time option (OM 17.09.2026)

OM F. No. Z.16025/227/2026/CGHS-III/EHS(8421134) dated 17.09.2026 — eligibility of serving Central Government employees for CGHS (immediate effect). It refers to OM No. C.14012/02/2018/CGHS-III/DIR dated 06.04.2018, under which CGHS coverage of serving employees was restricted to those residing / working within a 5 km radius of a CGHS Wellness Centre.

  • The geographical (5 km) criterion is totally dispensed with.
  • One-time option: serving employees residing / posted outside the earlier geographical coverage or in a city not covered by CGHS, who are on CS(MA) Rules solely for that reason, may opt to become CGHS beneficiaries, subject to other eligibility conditions and payment of the prescribed CGHS contribution.
  • Mandatory CGHS: serving employees residing or posted within the CGHS-covered area, i.e. the limits of the district headquarters where a CGHS Wellness Centre is situated, are mandatorily covered under CGHS and cannot opt out in favour of CS(MA).
  • Conditions of the option: one-time, final and binding; applies to all dependants (no splitting between the two systems); the employee keeps paying the CGHS contribution irrespective of residence / posting; no simultaneous claims under CGHS and CS(MA); no TA/DA for treatment or medicine procurement under CGHS rules; an undertaking that benefits will not be availed under both systems (inadmissible benefits are recoverable).
  • Employees who do not opt continue under CS(MA) Rules, 1944. False, incorrect or suppressed information attracts disciplinary action under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and recovery.

Effect on the exam answer: “CS(MA) applies where CGHS does not” is now only the default. A serving employee outside a CGHS area may choose CGHS once, irrevocably, for the whole family.

📜 Nature and Key Characteristics of CS(MA) Rules
  • Nature: Statutory Rules — made under the Government of India Act 1935 (continued under the Constitution of India). These are legally enforceable rights, unlike CGHS which is an executive scheme
  • Notified: 1st January 1944
  • Administered by: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Govt of India — through individual Ministries/Depts for their employees
  • Applicability Area: Applies to Central Govt employees posted in areas NOT covered by CGHS (i.e., non-CGHS cities and stations). Employees in CGHS cities are governed by CGHS, not CS(MA) Rules
  • Beneficiaries (Broad): Serving Central Govt employees + their dependent family members. Note: Retired Govt employees (pensioners) are EXCLUDED from CS(MA) Rules — pensioners are covered under CGHS (if enrolled) or FMA
  • Key linkage with CGHS: CS(MA) beneficiaries get treatment at CGHS rates from any CGHS-empanelled HCO [MoHFW OM 11.01.2011]. Emergency treatment in non-empanelled hospital: reimbursement at Non-NABH CGHS rates of nearest CGHS city
  • MoHFW website: https://main.mohfw.gov.in/documents/csma — has Circulars, Empanelled Hospital Lists, Forms

Hinglish — CS(MA) Rules ka Essence
🗣️ Hinglish — CS(MA) Rules ka Essence

CS(MA) Rules 1944 ek statutory framework hai — CGHS se fundamentally alag. CGHS ek executive scheme hai (guidelines + OMs se governed); CS(MA) Rules Government of India Act ke under bane statutory rules hain. CS(MA) Rules sirf non-CGHS cities mein posted employees ke liye hain. Retired officers (pensioners) ke liye CS(MA) Rules apply NAHI hote — woh CGHS ya FMA ke under aate hain.

⚠️ Most Important Trap — CS(MA) vs CGHS Applicability
  • "CS(MA) Rules apply to retired Govt servants" — WRONG! Rule 1 Note 2(iv): Retired Govt officials are EXCLUDED
  • "CS(MA) Rules apply to employees in Delhi" — WRONG! Employees in Delhi are covered under CGHS (Delhi = CGHS city)
  • "CGHS and CS(MA) apply together to same employee" — WRONG! Either CGHS (CGHS city employees) OR CS(MA) (non-CGHS areas) — not both
  • "CS(MA) Rules are executive guidelines" — WRONG! They are statutory rules made under GOI Act 1935

🆕 updated with 2026 orders
📊 Visual summary — diagrams & comparison
🆕 UPDATE — Rule 1 coverage — see OM 17.09.2026

A serving employee posted in a CGHS-covered area (district HQ limits where a Wellness Centre is situated) is mandatorily under CGHS and outside CS(MA); one outside such an area may opt once, irrevocably, for CGHS for the whole family; otherwise CS(MA) continues. Details: the update box in the CS(MA) preamble and the Latest orders tab.

🆕 UPDATE — Pensioners are outside CS(MA) — their three options (OM 12.09.2022)

MoHFW OM File No. S.14028/30/2022-EHS dated 12.09.2022 — reimbursement of medical claims to pensioners under CS(MA) Rules (as directed by CATs / courts):

  • Retired Government officials are not covered by the CS(MA) Rules (an earlier OM No. S.14025/23/2013-MS-EHSS dated 29.09.2016 said the same: the Rules “are not applicable to pensioners”).
  • Pensioners residing in non-CGHS areas have three options: (1) FMA in lieu of OPD; (2) CGHS (OPD & IPD) by registering at the nearest CGHS-covered city with the required subscription; (3) FMA for OPD and CGHS for IPD with subscription.
  • Ministries / Departments are to defend CAT / court cases in this light and need not refer them to MoHFW; retiring employees are to be made aware of the position.

This confirms the guide’s statement that pensioners are excluded from CS(MA) (the guide cites Rule 1 Note 2(iv); the OM calls it a note below Rule 2).

Read from the published text of the OM and the DoT copy reproducing the 2016 OM.

📜 Rule 1(2) — Applicability: Who is GENERALLY COVERED

These rules shall apply to all Government servants EXCEPT:

  • (i) Those in railway service
  • (ii) Those of non-Gazetted rank stationed in or passing through Calcutta whose conditions of service are prescribed by Central Government Rules

When covered: when they are on duty, leave or Foreign Service in India or when under suspension.

Explanation Explanation of "Foreign Service in India": When a Govt servant's pay is drawn from non-Central Govt sources (e.g., deputed to a PSU or State Govt) but is still within India.

📜 Rule 1 Note 2 — 8 Categories EXCLUDED from CS(MA) Rules

These rules do NOT apply to:

  • (i) Defence Services personnel
  • (ii) Government servants who are on leave or deputation abroad
  • (iii) Non-Gazetted Govt servants (including Group D) and Gazetted Govt servants other than Central Services Group A drawing pay < Rs.750 p.m., stationed in/passing through Calcutta — for whom special arrangements for medical attendance and/or treatment have been made
  • (iv) Retired Government Officials [This is the MOST examined exclusion]
  • (v) Non-Officials sent on deputation abroad
  • (vi) Government servants in Delhi/New Delhi who are governed by CGHS while in New Delhi
  • (vii) Officers of the All-India Services and other persons who are governed by the All-India Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1954
  • (viii) India-based officers and staff serving in Missions abroad — governed by the Assisted Medical Attendance Scheme

📜 Rule 1 Note 3 — 11 Categories INCLUDED Despite Seeming Exclusion

These rules apply to:

  • (i) All Central Government servants who are on leave preparatory to retirement, or on refused leave taken immediately after the date of compulsory retirement or on the expiry of an extension of service
  • (ii) Officers of the General Administrative Reserve
  • (iii) Government pensioners on their re-employment under the Central Government, irrespective of the service to which they belonged at the time of retirement
  • (iv) Defence Accounts Department personnel
  • (v) Civilians paid from Defence Service Estimates (with exceptions)
  • (vi) Central Government servants on terminal leave
  • (vii) A probationer
  • (viii) Apprentices who are in the whole time service of Government
  • (ix) [* * * * *] — omitted
  • (x) Police personnel including personnel of the Assam Rifles — subject to conditions specified in MoH OM No. R 13-10/53-LSG(M) dated 18.03.1954
  • (xi) All State Government servants on deputation with the Central Government

⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 1
  • "CS(MA) Rules apply to retired officials" — WRONG! Note 2(iv): EXCLUDED
  • "AIS officers come under CS(MA)" — WRONG! They have separate AIS (MA) Rules, 1954
  • "Railway employee on deputation to MoF is excluded" — WRONG! Note 1: INCLUDED during deputation
  • "Probationers not covered" — WRONG! Note 3(vii): INCLUDED
  • "Suspended officer loses medical benefits" — WRONG! Rule 1(2) covers when "under suspension"
  • "Defence Services employees covered under CS(MA)" — WRONG! Note 2(i): EXCLUDED (Defence Accounts personnel are included — that's different)
  • "Employee on leave preparatory to retirement = excluded" — WRONG! Note 3(i): INCLUDED

📜 Rule 2(a) — Authorised Medical Attendant (AMA): Complete Definition

Rule 2(a)(A) — Where a Medical Officer IS APPOINTED by Govt:

AMA means a Medical Officer, whether or not under the employ of the Central Government, appointed by:

  • 2(a)(A)(i): The Department of Health of the Government of India — where persons are under the employ of that Department
  • 2(a)(A)(ii): Any other Department of the Government of India — in relation to persons under the employ of that Department
  • 2(a)(A)(iii): Any authority declared by the President, under sub-rule (10) of Rule 2 of the Supplementary Rules, to be the Head of a Department — in relation to persons under that authority
  • 2(a)(A)(iv): The Chairman of the Central Government Employees Welfare Co-ordination Committee at stations where such Committees are functioning — in relation to CG employees at the station

Rule 2(a)(B) — Where NO Medical Officer is appointed as above:

  • 2(a)(B)(i): In respect of a Govt servant who belongs to Central Service, Group A, or whose pay is not less than Rs.2 per mensem (in 1944 terms; updated by GDs) — the Principal Medical Officer of the District appointed by the Govt to attend its officers
  • 2(a)(B)(ii): In respect of Group A servant whose pay is less than the above threshold — an Assistant Surgeon, Grade I (Medical Graduate) or other Medical Officer similarly appointed
  • 2(a)(B)(iii): In respect of any other Govt servant — an Assistant Surgeon, Grade II (Medical Licentiate) or where not available, an Assistant Surgeon Grade I

📜 Rule 2(a) Notes 1–5 (All Mandatory Notes)
  • Note Note 1: To determine the status of an officer, the actual pay he is drawing at the time he falls ill should be taken into account
  • Note Note 2: For the purpose of determination of status of an officer under suspension, the actual pay he was drawing just before the date of his suspension should be taken into account
  • Note Note 3: In the case of re-employed pensioners, the pension should be taken into consideration along with pay for the purpose of determining the grade for medical attendance and treatment
  • Note Note 4: The authorised medical attendant of a Govt servant is determined with reference to the place at which he falls ill — whether it be his permanent residence, or place of casual stay, or the place where he may be spending his leave
  • Note Note 5: Honorary Medical Officers outside hospital precincts are just like private medical practitioners and so cannot be regarded as authorised medical attendants of the CG employees, under the rules. (Exception: In Andhra States, however, honorary medical officers have been declared as authorised medical attendants)

🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 2(a) — AMA Appointment
  • GD(1) — 5 km radius rule: When adequate numbers of Government doctors or their services are not available in various systems of medicine within a radius of 5 kms (8 km by some references), private registered medical practitioners would be appointed as AMA
  • GD(2) — HoD appointment of private AMA: Head of Departments can issue appointment orders to Private Medical Practitioner as AMA after verifying the duly filled prescribed proforma with proper verification of antecedents through local police
  • GD(3) — Annual re-verification of AMA: Annual re-verification of doctors appointed as AMA under CS(MA) Rules is mandatory [MoHFW OM — see mohfw.gov.in/csma]
  • GD(4) — NABH/NABL accreditation: NABH/NABL accreditation of hospitals/diagnostic centers recognized as AMA under CS(MA) [MoHFW OM]
  • GD(5) — Suspension case: Govt employee under suspension is entitled to reimbursement of medical expenses at par with working employees
  • GD(6) — Both spouses as Govt employees: Both husband and wife who are Govt employees can claim reimbursement of medical expenses for their respective parents
  • GD(7) — Female employee option (parents/parents-in-law): Now extended to both male and female employees — can choose either parents OR parents-in-law [OM 26.07.2023; extended to CS(MA) by OM 28.03.2024]
  • GD(8) — One-time irrevocable choice: Male Govt employee can exercise ONE-TIME OPTION ONLY for choosing parents or parents-in-law — cannot be changed later [MoHFW OM 13.05.2026]
  • GD(9) — 2-child restriction NOT applicable: Restriction of two children is NOT applicable for claiming medical reimbursement
  • GD(10) — Disability definitions: For determining permanent disability: (a) Blindness; (b) Low vision; (c) Leprosy cured; (d) Hearing impairment; (e) Locomotor disability; (f) Mental retardation; (g) Mental illness
📜 Rule 2(b) — "District"

"District" means the district in which the Government servant falls ill.

Explanation Explanation: This is critical — the AMA, hospital entitlement, etc. are all determined with reference to the district WHERE the servant falls ill — NOT the district of posting or home district.

📜 Rule 2(c) — "Family" (For CS(MA) Rules)

Family for CS(MA) Rules includes:

  • (i) Husband or wife as the case may be — NO dependency condition for spouse
  • (ii) Wholly dependent/minor children: Unmarried son up to age 25 years; unmarried daughter — no age limit
  • Widowed daughters — no age limit
  • Son suffering from any permanent disability — irrespective of age limit
  • Dependent divorced/separated daughters — irrespective of age limit
  • (iii) Sisters — unmarried or widowed sister — no age limit (wholly dependent)
  • (iv) Dependent parents OR parents-in-law — income from all sources < Rs.9,000 + DA per month ➕ [Source verified: MoHFW OM No. S-11012/2/2016-CGHS-P dated 08.11.2016 — this OM explicitly extends the Rs.9,000+DA CGHS income-dependency threshold to CS(MA) Rules cases too, para 6] — 🔄 current computed figure at DA/DR = 63% (effective 01.07.2026): ≈ Rs.14,670/month (Rs.9,000 + Rs.5,670 DA); recompute at each DA revision (next due 01.01.2027) — normally residing with employee [Condition: one-time irrevocable choice — OM 13.05.2026]
  • (v) Dependent minor brother(s) — up to age of becoming major (18 years)
  • (vi) Dependent transgender children and siblings — irrespective of age limit [CS(MA) Rules Amendment — OM dated 16.09.2025; requires Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 certificate]

Dependent minor children of widowed/separated daughters: Also covered — up to age of becoming major

📜 Rule 2(d) — "Medical Attendance"

"Medical Attendance" means attendance:

  • (i) At a hospital (OPD)
  • (ii) At the residence of the Government servant
  • (iii) At the consulting room of the AMA — whether at the hospital or at his own residence

Included in Medical Attendance: Consultation; prescription of medicines; taking of pathological/bacteriological specimens; X-ray; laboratory investigations; preventive care; administration of injections; dressings

📜 Rule 2(h) — "Treatment"

"Treatment" means the use of all medical and surgical facilities available at the Government hospital in which the Government servant is treated.

Treatment includes:

  • (i) The employment of such pathological, bacteriological, radiological or other methods as are considered necessary by the AMA
  • (ii) All nursing care available in the hospital
  • (iii) Medicines, surgical appliances, and other supplies available in the hospital
  • (iv) Diet of the patient in the hospital

Note Note: "Treatment" in the hospital sense = the entire package of services at a Govt hospital — distinct from "Medical Attendance" which is the OPD consultation at AMA's consulting room.

⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 2
  • "AMA determined by place of posting" — WRONG! Determined by place where servant FALLS ILL [Note 4]
  • "District = home district of employee" — WRONG! District = where servant falls ill
  • "Honorary MO outside hospital = AMA" — WRONG! Note 5: honorary MOs outside hospital precincts = private practitioners (except Andhra States)
  • "For suspended officer, current suspension pay determines AMA grade" — WRONG! Note 2: pay drawn just before suspension
  • "Medical Attendance includes indoor treatment" — WRONG! Medical Attendance = OPD; Treatment = indoor/hospital
  • "Both parents AND parents-in-law can be included as dependents" — WRONG! Only ONE set — one-time irrevocable choice [OM 13.05.2026]
  • "2-child restriction applies under CS(MA)" — WRONG! GD(9): NOT applicable
  • "Transgender dependents must be below 25 for CS(MA)" — WRONG! Any age [CS(MA) Amendment 16.09.2025]

🔴 Critical — Foundation Entitlement Rule
📜 Rule 3(i) — Free Medical Attendance Entitlement

A Government servant shall be entitled, free of charge, to medical attendance by the authorised medical attendant.

Scope of free medical attendance:

  • Consultation by AMA at OPD/hospital/residence/consulting room
  • Prescriptions by AMA
  • Pathological/bacteriological/radiological examinations ordered by AMA at Govt hospital
  • Administration of injections, dressings by AMA
  • Medicines included in the Schedule (formulary)

📜 Rule 3(ii) — Reimbursement When Paid by Servant

Where a Government servant is entitled under Rule 3(i) to receive medical attendance free of charge, any amount paid by him on account of such medical attendance shall, on production of a certificate in writing by the AMA in this behalf, be reimbursed to him by the Central Government.

Condition: AMA must provide written certificate that the medical attendance was necessary and was in fact provided.

🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 3
  • GD(1) — AYUSH (Indian System of Medicine): An AMA under Indian System of Medicine (Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy, Yoga) may provide medical attendance for a maximum period of 40 days in a single continuous spell of illness. Beyond 40 days, referral to Govt hospital needed.
  • GD(2) — Combined period with specialist: The combined total period of medical attendance by AMA + specialist should in all jointly be limited to 10 days for a single continuous spell of illness (for allopathic AMA). Specialist consultation beyond 4 consultations within 10 days → patient referred to OPD of Govt/recognized hospital.
  • GD(3) — Controlling Officer's powers of rejection: The Controlling Officer in Ministries/Departments is fully empowered to reject any medical claim which does not satisfy the genuineness and other requirements under the provisions of the rules — without consulting MoHFW. Cases requiring clarification/interpretation → referred to MoHFW.
  • GD(4) — Appeal against rejection: When the medical reimbursement claim of an employee is rejected by the Controlling Officer and reasons communicated to the claimant, the claimant may submit an appeal to the Central Government within 45 days from the date of receipt of the rejection order.
  • GD(5) — Prescription validity: The medical prescription issued by AMA/Govt Specialist for diagnostic test/investigation is valid for single use within a period of 2 weeks (14 days) from the date of prescription, unless specified by them in the prescription. For chronic/long-term illness: valid for 6 months.
  • GD(6) — Investigation validity: Prescription for investigations is valid for 30 days from date of prescription (single use).
Hinglish — Rule 3
🗣️ Hinglish — Rule 3
  • Rule 3(i): AMA se OPD treatment FREE milegi — koi charges nahi
  • Rule 3(ii): Agar apne paisa diya → AMA ka written certificate lao → government wapas karega
  • AYUSH AMA limit: 40 din maximum per illness. Usse zyada → refer to Govt hospital
  • Prescription validity: 14 din (2 weeks) normal; 30 din for investigations; 6 months for chronic illness
  • Rejection appeal: 45 din mein Central Govt ko appeal karo
  • Controlling Officer: Claim reject kar sakta hai bina MoHFW se puchhe — par reasons batane hote hain
⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 3
  • "No AMA certificate needed for reimbursement under Rule 3" — WRONG! Written certificate of AMA mandatory
  • "AYUSH AMA can treat for any duration" — WRONG! Maximum 40 days
  • "Appeal against rejection: 60 days" — WRONG! 45 days
  • "Prescription valid for 30 days always" — WRONG! Normal prescription: 14 days; Investigations: 30 days; Chronic: 6 months
  • "Controlling Officer needs MoHFW permission to reject claim" — WRONG! Fully empowered to reject independently
🚗 E. Rule 4 — Travelling Allowance for Medical Attendance Journeys
Rule 4

Rule 4 — TA for Medical Attendance: 5-Mile (8 km) Rule, When Patient Pays vs AMA Pays, Certificate Requirement

Rule 4(1)(a)(b) | Rule 4(2) | Distance threshold | AMA's TA entitlement | Certificate requirement
📊 Visual summary — diagrams & comparison
🟠 High Priority
📜 Rule 4(1) — When TA is Admissible

When the place at which a patient falls ill is more than five miles (approximately 8 km) by the shortest route from the consulting room of the AMA:

  • Rule 4(1)(a) — Patient travels to AMA: The patient shall be entitled to travelling allowance for the journey to and from the AMA's consulting room
  • Rule 4(1)(b) — Patient too ill to travel: If the patient is too ill to travel, the AMA shall be entitled to travelling allowance for the journey to and from the place where the patient is

Distance calculation: The 5 miles/8 km is measured by the shortest route — not the route actually taken by the patient/AMA.

Aur agar patient itna beemar hai ki AMA ke paas ja nahi sakta, to AMA ko patient ke paas aane ka TA milta hai. Yani TA dono direction mein possible hai — distance ya illness ke basis par.

🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 4 — TA Rules
  • GD(1) — Within CGHS city: For CGHS employees/CS(MA) beneficiaries referred as outpatients to recognized hospitals in the same city — no conveyance charges payable even if distance is more than 8 km. [CSIR circular based on CGHS principle]
  • GD(2) — Compounders/Lab Assistants: Compounders and Lab Assistants of AMA are NOT eligible for TA when accompanying the AMA
  • GD(3) — Scale of TA: The scale of TA admissible is the same as for journey on duty at the relevant pay scale of the employee
  • GD(4) — Special TA for TB/Cancer patients: TB patients and cancer patients are given special TA concessions:
    • Patient + Attendant: Both entitled to half of normal journey fare
    • Patient alone (no attendant): One quarter of normal journey fare

Rule 5 — Specialist Consultation: AMA Referral, 4-Consultation-10-Day Rule, Second Specialist, TA Entitlement

📜 Rule 5(1) — AMA Referral to Specialist

If the AMA is of opinion that the case of a patient is of such a serious or special nature as to require medical attendance by some person other than himself, he may:

  • Rule 5(1)(a): Refer the patient to a specialist or other medical officer at a Government hospital, paid by Government, or stationed in the district — for specialist consultation to such extent as the specialist/MO may determine in consultation with AMA
  • Rule 5(1)(b): If no such specialist is available at or near the place where the patient falls ill — the AMA may refer the patient to a specialist or MO at any Government hospital that can be reasonably reached
  • Rule 5(1)(c): If no specialist is available as per (a) or (b) — refer to a private specialist (with AMA's certificate that no Govt specialist is available)

📜 Rule 5(2) — Second Specialist

If the AMA or the first specialist is of opinion that a second specialist opinion is needed, the patient may be referred to another specialist. The entitlement and procedure are the same as under Rule 5(1).

📜 Rule 5(3) — Travelling Allowance for Specialist Consultation

When a patient is referred to a specialist under Rule 5(1) or 5(2):

  • If patient travels to the specialist: Patient entitled to TA for the journey (same principle as Rule 4)
  • If patient is too ill to travel: The specialist is entitled to TA for the journey to the patient's location

🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 5 — Specialist Consultation
  • GD(1) — 4 Consultations in 10 Days Rule:
    • (a) First four consultations/visits should be completed within a period of 10 days from the date of commencement of treatment in respect of one single and continuous spell of illness in respect of a particular disease
    • If the specialist considers it necessary beyond 4 consultations → refer patient to OPD of Govt/recognized hospital for continuing treatment
    • (b) In Indian System of Medicine and Homoeopathy — the 10-day limit may be increased up to 40 days by AMA
  • GD(2) — Fresh vs Subsequent Consultation:
    • Every consultation after the first for the same illness = "subsequent consultation"
    • After being cured of a particular illness, patient develops a fresh illness and consults the same doctor → treated as "fresh consultation"
    • Where patient consults the same doctor for superimposition of another disease during the course of treatment of one disease → treated as "fresh consultation"
  • GD(3) — Specialist should NOT name a specific hospital: Government specialist shall NOT refer beneficiaries to any particular empanelled hospital by name but should specify the treatment and mention "referred to any empanelled hospital"
  • GD(4) — AMA Consultation Fees [OM No. S.11025/18/2023-EHS dated 20.09.2023]:
    • Medical Post Graduate/Specialists: First consultation Rs.350/-; Subsequent consultation Rs.350/-
    • MBBS doctors: First consultation Rs.200/-; Subsequent consultation Rs.200/-
    • Injection charges: Intramuscular/Subcutaneous Rs.25/-; Intravenous Rs.50/-
    • Important: No separate charges for day and night consultation — uniform rates at all times [OM 20.09.2023]
    • These orders supersede all earlier orders on consultation fees
  • GD(5) — Male child in women's hospital: A male child of a Government servant is allowed to receive medical attendance and treatment in a recognised women's hospital till the age of 6 years
  • GD(6) — Prescription validity for Specialist referral: AMA prescription for specialist consultation valid for single use within 2 weeks. Specialist prescription for investigations valid for 30 days. Chronic illness prescription from specialist: 6 months.
Hinglish — Rule 5
🗣️ Hinglish — Rule 5
  • AMA refer karta hai: AMA ne soch liya ki specialist chahiye → Govt hospital ka specialist ko refer karo → pehle Govt, phir private (only if no Govt available)
  • 4 in 10 days: Specialist se 4 consultations → 10 din ke andar. Zyada zaroori ho → Govt hospital OPD mein refer karo. AYUSH mein → 40 days limit
  • Fresh vs Subsequent: Same bimari = subsequent. Nayi bimari = fresh. Ek bimari ke upar doosri bimari = fresh consultation
  • AMA fees (2023 revised): Specialist/PG first = Rs.350; subsequent = Rs.350. MBBS first = Rs.200; subsequent = Rs.200. Day/night = same rate (no extra)
  • Male child in women's hospital: 6 saal tak
⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 5
  • "4 consultations per illness total" — WRONG! 4 consultations within 10 days
  • "Specialist can name a specific hospital" — WRONG! Only "any empanelled hospital" — not by name
  • "Night consultation fee is extra" — WRONG! No separate day/night charges [OM 20.09.2023]
  • "MBBS AMA first consultation = Rs.350" — WRONG! MBBS = Rs.200; Specialist/PG = Rs.350
  • "Male child cannot be treated in women's hospital" — WRONG! Allowed till age 6 years
  • "AYUSH AMA also limited to 4 consultations in 10 days" — WRONG! AYUSH limit is 40 days
  • "Same doctor fresh consultation after cure of illness = subsequent" — WRONG! After cure of a PARTICULAR illness, fresh illness = fresh consultation

🆕 UPDATE — HoD permission for private-hospital treatment & emergency reimbursement (OM 05.06.2014)

MoHFW OM No. S.14025/01/2014-MS dated 05.06.2014 (IFD concurrence CD No. 335 dated 28.05.2014) — delegation to Heads of Departments for CS(MA) beneficiaries. Read in a Department of Posts letter of 25.11.2021 that reproduces it

  • A serving employee covered under CS(MA) who is being treated at a Government hospital and wants treatment in a private hospital recognised under CGHS / CS(MA): the Head of Department may grant permission for indoor treatment on the prescription of the concerned AMA.
  • Heads of Departments may decide reimbursement of emergency treatment at a private hospital / nursing home / clinic, subject to item-wise ceiling as per CGHS / CS(MA) rates.
  • Departments / Ministries settle all cases with no relaxation of rules where entitlement is worked out from the prescribed rate list: Heads up to Rs.2,00,000; above that (still per rate list) in consultation with the Internal Finance Division; only cases needing relaxation of rules go to MoHFW.

The letter adds that MoHFW (ID No. S.14025/35/2021-EHS dated 29.10.2021) clarified that the 2014 OM remains valid for CS(MA) beneficiaries, and that the Rs.5 lakh enhancement of OM 23.11.2016 was noted as applying to CGHS beneficiary cases. OM 16.02.2026 now sets the HoD ceiling at Rs.10 lakh for settlement “under CGHS or CS(MA) Rules”.

🔴 Critical — Emergency Reimbursement Rate is Key
📜 Rule 6(1) — Entitlement to Free Inpatient Treatment

A Govt servant is entitled, free of charge, to treatment in a hospital:

  • Rule 6(1)(a): In such Government hospital at or near the place where he falls ill as can provide the necessary and suitable treatment — in the opinion of the AMA
  • Rule 6(1)(b): If no such Govt hospital is available at or near the place — in such hospital other than a Government hospital at or near the place as can provide the necessary and suitable treatment — in the opinion of the AMA [This covers recognized private hospitals under CS(MA) Rules]
  • Rule 6(1)(c): Where a Govt servant falls ill at a place other than his headquarters and where AMA opinion cannot be obtained — the head of the nearest Government hospital shall determine the appropriate hospital

📜 Rule 6(2) — Reimbursement When Employee Pays

Where a Govt servant is entitled under Rule 6(1) to free treatment in a hospital, any amount paid by him on account of such treatment shall, on production of a certificate in writing by the AMA, be reimbursed to him by the Central Government.

Note Note: If the Controlling Authority rejects the claim, the claimant may submit an appeal within 45 days of the date of receipt of the rejection order.

Worked Example: Worked example: Order/prescription ki trigger date note karke applicable 14-day/45-day deadline calendar mein mark karo.

🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 6 — Hospitalization
  • GD(1) — CS(MA) beneficiaries at CGHS rates [MoHFW OM 11.01.2011]: CS(MA) beneficiaries and their dependent family members can get treatment at CGHS rates from any HCO recognized under CGHS. Reimbursement: as per prescribed CGHS rate list of nearest CGHS covered city or actual, whichever lower.
  • GD(2) — Emergency treatment in non-empanelled private hospital [MoHFW OM S.14025/14/2012-MS]: Reimbursement of medical expenses incurred in emergency conditions at non-empanelled private hospital — allowed as per prevailing Non-NABH CGHS rates of the CGHS covered city (or nearest CGHS city for non-CGHS places) or actual, whichever is less. Package rates (CGHS non-NABH) apply where CGHS rates prescribed.
  • GD(3) — HoD permission for private hospital treatment [MoHFW OM]: A serving CG employee covered under CS(MA) Rules who is taking treatment at Govt hospital and desires to obtain treatment at a private hospital recognized under CGHS/CS(MA) Rules — the Head of Department may grant him permission for indoor treatment on the basis of medical prescription issued by the AMA.
  • GD(4) — Emergency cases — HoD decides [delegation]: Powers to decide cases falling under "emergency" category — delegated to Heads of Departments in various Ministries/Departments for settling permission cases and for approval relating to medical reimbursement under CS(MA) Rules [MoHFW OM on delegation].
  • GD(5) — Mental illness indoor treatment: A patient may be allowed to receive indoor treatment for a maximum period of 3 years for mental diseases.
  • GD(6) — Claim time limit: Final claim for reimbursement of medical expenses (CS(MA)) to be submitted within 6 months of discharge from hospital or within 6 months of treatment taken (OPD). [CGHS limit is also 6 months since OM 01.06.2020]
  • GD(7) — Cancer treatment [MoHFW OM]: CS(MA) beneficiaries permitted to get treatment from any cancer treatment hospital — reimbursement limited to CGHS rates or actual, whichever less. Permission from HoD/Head of CGHS city for specific treatment procedures.
  • GD(8) — Empanelment of hospitals [MoHFW]: Test/Investigation of private hospitals/diagnostic laboratories/imaging centers empanelled under CS(MA) Rules — separate guidelines issued. NABH/NABL accreditation encouraged.
  • GD(9) — HoD delegation for MRC settlement [CGHS OM 16.02.2026]: Powers delegated to HoDs for settling permission cases and post-facto approval relating to Referral System and Medical Reimbursement under CS(MA) Rules 1944.
Hinglish — Rule 6
🗣️ Hinglish — Rule 6
  • Free treatment: Govt hospital → if not available → recognized private hospital. AMA ki opinion se decide hoga.
  • Emergency mein non-empanelled private hospital: Non-NABH CGHS rates ya actual — jo kam ho. Emergency certificate chahiye.
  • CS(MA) beneficiaries CGHS empanelled hospitals mein CGHS rates par treatment le sakte hain [OM 11.01.2011]
  • Mental illness: Max 3 saal indoor treatment
  • Claim: 6 months mein submit karo (CGHS bhi ab 6 months hai — OM 01.06.2020)
  • HoD ke paas powers hain private hospital permission dene ke liye aur emergency claims settle karne ke liye
⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 6
  • "CS(MA) claim within 3 months" — WRONG! CS(MA) = 6 months (CGHS is also 6 months since OM 01.06.2020)
  • "Emergency reimbursement at NABH rates" — WRONG! At Non-NABH CGHS rates of nearest CGHS city or actual, whichever less
  • "Private hospitals in CGHS cities can be empanelled under CS(MA)" — WRONG! Only private hospitals in non-CGHS covered cities
  • "Mental illness: no limit on indoor treatment" — WRONG! Maximum 3 years
  • "AMA certificate not needed for hospitalization reimbursement" — WRONG! Written AMA certificate is mandatory
🏠 H. Rule 7 — Treatment at Residence
Rule 7

Rule 7 — Treatment at Residence: When Permitted, Entitlement & Certificate Requirement

Rule 7(1) | Rule 7(2) | Rule 7(3)(a)(b) | AMA's certificate of necessity
📊 Visual summary — diagrams & comparison
🟠 High Priority
📜 Rule 7(1) — When Treatment at Residence is Permitted

If the AMA is of the opinion that owing to:

  • (a) The absence or remoteness of a suitable hospital — i.e., no suitable hospital is available near the patient's location; OR
  • (b) The severity of the illness — patient cannot be removed to the hospital

→ A Government servant may receive treatment at his residence.

Both conditions are alternatives — either absence of hospital OR severity of illness is sufficient.

Dono cases mein AMA ki opinion se ghar par treatment permitted hota hai. Yani hospital possible ho to ghar ka ilaaj nahi — sirf in 2 conditions mein.

📜 Rule 7(2) — Entitlement for Residence Treatment

A Government servant receiving treatment at his residence under Rule 7(1) shall be entitled to receive towards the cost of such treatment incurred by him a sum equivalent to the cost of similar treatment in a hospital — i.e., the same entitlement as if treated in a hospital.

Explanation Explanation: The entitlement does NOT exceed what would have been the cost in a Govt hospital. Patient gets the hospital-equivalent benefit even at home.

📜 Rule 7(3) — Certificate Requirements for Residence Treatment

Claims for sums admissible under Rule 7(2) shall be accompanied by a certificate in writing by the AMA stating:

  • Rule 7(3)(a): His reasons for the opinion referred to in Rule 7(1) — i.e., WHY hospital treatment was not possible (remote hospital / severity of illness)
  • Rule 7(3)(b): The cost of similar treatment in a hospital — to cap the reimbursement at equivalent hospital rates

🔵 Government Decision under Rule 7
  • GD(1): It may be reiterated that reimbursement of expenses incurred on treatment obtained in the private clinics/nursing homes of the AMA would NOT be admissible under Rule 7 or in relaxation of CS(MA) Rules — even in emergent cases. Rule 7 is for actual residence of patient, not AMA's private clinic.
  • GD(2) — What is admissible at residence: Medicines; AMA visits; injections; dressings; minor procedures — all at hospital-equivalent rates. Ayah/nursing charges at residence — separate provisions under Rule 8.

  • "Treatment at AMA's private clinic = treatment at residence" — WRONG! GD(1): AMA's clinic NOT covered under Rule 7

  • "Entitlement at residence is limited to medicine cost only" — WRONG! Same as hospital-equivalent treatment entitlement
  • "Only one certificate needed" — WRONG! Certificate needs both: (a) reasons for residence treatment AND (b) equivalent hospital cost

🔴 Critical — Densest Rule; All Sub-Rules Examinable
📜 Rule 8(1) — Charges Not Included in Medical Attendance/Treatment

Charges for services rendered in connection with but NOT included in medical attendance on, or treatment of, a patient entitled free of charge to medical attendance or treatment under these Rules — shall be determined by the AMA and paid by the patient.

Examples of non-included charges: Charges for companions, telephone calls, special foods beyond prescribed diet, laundry, TV, newspapers, etc.

📜 Rule 8(2) — Final Authority on What is Included

If any question arises as to whether any service is included in medical attendance or treatment, it shall be referred to the Government and the decision of the Government shall be FINAL.

Explanation Explanation: No one except the Government (MoHFW) can determine finally whether a particular service is covered. The AMA's opinion is not final on this question.

📜 Government Decision / OM made under Rule 8(2) — Dental Treatment

Dental treatment can be availed by CS(MA) beneficiaries in any private hospital recognized under CGHS/CS(MA) Rules or State Govt hospitals.

Admissible under the relevant Government Decision / OM made under Rule 8(2):

  • Extraction of teeth
  • Scaling
  • Gum treatment
  • Fillings
  • Root Canal Treatment (RCT)
  • Complete denture — ceiling: Rs.2,000/- (as revised)

NOT Admissible: Orthodontic treatment (braces, aligners, retainers, etc.)

Empanelment: Guidelines for empanelment of dental hospitals/clinics under CS(MA) Rules available on MoHFW website.

📜 Government Decision / OM made under Rule 8(2) — Maternity and Confinement

Confinement, pre-natal and post-natal treatment means treatment received by the wife of a Govt servant (or female Govt servant herself) before and after child-birth for physiological or other disability attributable to child-birth.

  • Antenatal care: Admissible
  • Confinement (delivery): Admissible at recognized hospitals — HoD may permit confinement at private recognized hospital
  • Postnatal care: Admissible
  • Note Note: Emergency Certificate for maternity is NOT a valid ground for using a private clinic/nursing home unless genuinely an emergency
  • Claims within 6 months of discharge

📜 Government Decision / OM made under Rule 8(2) — Ambulance Charges

Reimbursable subject to conditions:

  • Treating doctor must certify: "Conveyance by any other mode would definitely endanger the patient's life or would grossly aggravate the condition"
  • OM No. S.4924/2010/CGHS(R&H)/CGHS(P) dated 17.01.2011 (applicable to CS(MA) also)
  • Reimbursable within the city only — inter-city ambulance subject to special consideration
  • NOT reimbursable: Ambulance for routine transport or when other modes of conveyance were available

📜 Government Decision / OM under Rule 8(2) — Eyesight Testing for Glasses
  • Government servants may have their eyesight tested for glasses at a Government/recognized hospital — once in every 3 years on the recommendation of the AMA
  • Above concession does NOT include provision of spectacles at Government expense — only the testing is covered, not the spectacles/frames/lenses
  • Family members are NOT entitled to the above concession [CS(MA) Rule book Page 210, Para 13]
  • Fee paid to the specialist for testing will be reimbursed [Rule 5 GD: "Once in every three years on the recommendations of the AMA. Fee paid to the specialist will be reimbursed"]

⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 8
  • "Orthodontic treatment admissible under the relevant Government Decision / OM made under Rule 8(2)" — WRONG! Orthodontic = NOT admissible
  • "Family members entitled to eyesight testing" — WRONG! Only employee; once in 3 years
  • "Spectacles covered at Govt expense" — WRONG! Only TESTING; spectacles NOT covered
  • "Annual medical exam for all Govt servants" — WRONG! Only Group A, age 40+
  • "Annual exam ceiling for men = Rs.2,200" — WRONG! Men = Rs.2,000; Women = Rs.2,200
  • "Mental illness: no limit on indoor treatment" — WRONG! Maximum 3 years
  • "IVF for all married women" — WRONG! Only married WOMAN GOVT SERVANT aged 21-39
  • "Government's decision on whether service included is advisory" — WRONG! FINAL and binding [Rule 8(2)]
  • "Cochlear implant = Rs.3 lakh" — WRONG! Rs.7,00,000 (pre-lingual) / Rs.6,00,000 (post-lingual), incl. GST [OM 09.11.2026]
  • "AICD covered like pacemaker" — WRONG! AICD specifically excluded
  • "Stents: max 2 per patient" — WRONG! Maximum 3 stents; costliest DES ceiling Rs.29,000 [OM 24.03.2023]

🆕 UPDATE — Claim time limit — CGHS and CS(MA) are both 6 months

CGHS final claims were also moved to 6 months by OM 01.06.2020 (see the update box in the CGHS reimbursement section). A delay beyond 6 months needs condonation.

🟠 High Priority
📜 Rule 9 — Counter-Signature and Claim Submission
  • Medical certificates issued by AMA and claims submitted by the Govt servant must be counter-signed/verified by the Controlling Officer
  • The Controlling Officer in the Ministry/Department is empowered to reject any medical claim that does not satisfy genuineness and other requirements — without consulting MoHFW
  • Cases requiring clarification/interpretation of rules or where Controlling Officer is satisfied the claim deserves consideration in relaxation → referred to MoHFW
  • Claim submission to Controlling Officer within 6 months of discharge/treatment (under CS(MA) Rules)
  • Claim for OPD treatment: Within 6 months of treatment date
  • Claim for advance: Submit final claim within 1 month of discharge from hospital (in case of advance drawn)

🌍 K. Rule 10 — Transfer to Foreign Service
Rule 10

Rule 10 — Medical Attendance on Transfer to Foreign Service (Deputation to PSU/State Govt/Autonomous Bodies)

Rule 10 | Foreign Service definition | Cost borne by | Special provisions
🔵 Medium Priority
📜 Rule 10 — Medical Facilities on Foreign Service

"Foreign Service" under these Rules = when a Govt servant serves in an organization outside the Central Govt (like PSU, State Govt, International Organization) — but his salary is paid from sources other than Central Govt estimates, even while remaining in India.

  • When a Govt servant is on Foreign Service in India, the cost of medical attendance and treatment shall be borne by the body/organization to which the Govt servant has been deputed (i.e., the foreign employer)
  • The Govt servant retains the same entitlements as per CS(MA) Rules — but the foreign employer pays
  • The scale of expenditure and eligibility for treatment = identical to the scale applicable to an official of the Indian Foreign Service of the corresponding grade in the Ministry of External Affairs under any Assisted Medical Attendance Scheme for the time being in force [Note: This provision has since been updated by specific OMs]
  • The Govt servant's service conditions (including medical entitlements) during foreign service = as per the terms of deputation agreed between the two organizations

📜 Rule 11(1) — Eligibility for Treatment Outside India

A Government servant shall be eligible to obtain medical treatment outside India and to claim reimbursement of the cost of medical treatment obtained inside or outside India in accordance with the provisions of this rule.

Condition: Treatment must be for conditions specified in the Table under Rule 11(3) AND must be recommended by the Standing Committee as per Rule 11(2).

📜 Rule 11(2) — Standing Committee: Constitution & Functions

For the purpose of this rule, a Standing Committee shall be established consisting of:

  • High-ranking medical and administrative officials
  • Typically: Director General of Health Services + other senior medical officials + senior admin officials from MoHFW

Functions of Standing Committee:

  • Consider applications for medical treatment outside India
  • Call for medical records, reports from specialists
  • Obtain second opinions where necessary
  • Determine whether the treatment falls within the specified conditions
  • Recommend whether treatment outside India is necessary

Application procedure: Govt servant desirous of treatment outside India shall apply through the Ministry/Department under which he is attached, to the Standing Committee, in the form specified by the Standing Committee.

Proforma: Proforma for treatment abroad cases under Rule 11 of CS(MA) Rules available on MoHFW website → CS(MA) → Forms and Downloads.

📜 Rule 11(3) — Specified Treatments Eligible for Outside India

Government servant is eligible for medical treatment outside India for conditions specified in the Table to this sub-rule. These include:

  • Advanced cardiovascular surgeries not available/feasible in India
  • Bone marrow transplants (in specific high-risk categories)
  • Certain complex oncological disorders
  • Treatments that fall in "high risk category" and are not available in India
  • [Full list as per Schedule/Table to Rule 11(3) — available on MoHFW website]

📜 Rule 11(4) — Government's Power to Revise List

It shall be competent for the Central Government to review from time to time the list of treatment facilities as specified in the Table to Rule 11(3) and make such additions or deletions as it may deem fit by notification in the Official Gazette.

Explanation Explanation: The list is not static — Government can add new treatments as medical technology advances or delete as these become available in India.

📜 Rule 11(5) — Prior Approval Requirement (Mandatory)

Prior approval of Standing Committee is MANDATORY before availing treatment outside India. The Ministry/Dept, on the strength of the certificate from the Standing Committee, shall incur necessary expenditure in getting the Govt servant or family member treated outside India in accordance with the procedure laid down by the Standing Committee.

Important: Treatment cannot begin outside India without prior clearance from the Standing Committee.

Hinglish: Reimbursement procedure ka yeh detail: Concerned Ministry/Department, par certificate (pramaan patra) se Standing Committee (sthayi samiti), hoga incur necessary kharcha ke liye getting sarkari karmchari ya member of his family ilaaj kiya jaata hai videsh mein ke mutabik procedure (chikitsa prakriya) laid down dwara Standing Committee (sthayi samiti). kharcha claimed zaroor supported dwara Standing Committee (sthayi samiti) certificate (pramaan patra). Yaad rakho: sequence = approval → treatment → bills → claim.
📜 Rule 11(7) — CG Discretionary Power (Exception to Prior Approval)

It shall be competent for the Central Government to authorize reimbursement for treatments obtained abroad if prior approval was not feasible due to circumstances beyond the servant's control (e.g., emergency abroad, impossibility of contacting Standing Committee in time).

Explanation Explanation: This is an exception provision. Generally, prior approval is mandatory. But if genuinely not possible to obtain prior approval (e.g., sudden emergency while already abroad), the CG can still authorize reimbursement retroactively.

Original Rule 11(7) — CG Discretionary Power (Exception to Prior Approval): Yeh parent original text hai; iske neeche ke saare sub-points isi provision ke under read honge.
Hinglish: Rule 11(7) — Central Government ki discretionary power (exception). Agar genuinely prior approval possible nahi tha (jaise achanak serious condition mein emergency travel), to Central Government apne discretion se post-facto reimbursement authorize kar sakti hai. Yeh Rule 11(5) ka exception hai — discretionary, right nahi.
Original authorize reimbursement for treatments obtained abroad: It shall be competent for the Central Government to authorize reimbursement for treatments obtained abroad if prior approval was not feasible due to circumstances beyond the servant's control (e.g., emergency abroad, impossibility of contacting Standing Committee in time).
Hinglish: CG discretion ka yeh point: It hoga competent ke liye Central Government (Kendriya Sarkar) se authorize reimbursement (kharcha wapas milna) ke liye treatments praapt kiya videsh mein agar pehle se approval (anumati) NAHI tha feasible due se circumstances beyond servant's control (jaise, emergency (aapatkaal) videsh mein, impossibility of contacting Standing Committee (sthayi samiti) mein time). Exam point: Rule 11(7) = exception to prior approval; CG ka discretion — har case mein nahi milta.
Original Explanation: This is an exception provision. Generally, prior approval is mandatory. But if genuinely not possible to obtain prior approval (e.g., sudden emergency while already abroad), the CG can still authorize reimbursement retroactively.
Hinglish: CG discretion ka yeh point: This hai an apvaad provision. aam taur par, pehle se approval (anumati) hai mandatory (zaroori). lekin agar genuinely NAHI possible se obtain pehle se approval (anumati) (jaise, sudden emergency (aapatkaal) while already videsh mein), CG sakta hai still authorize reimbursement (kharcha wapas milna) retroactively. Exam point: Rule 11(7) = exception to prior approval; CG ka discretion — har case mein nahi milta.
🔵 Government Decisions under Rule 11
  • GD(1) — Scale of treatment abroad: The scale of expenditure and eligibility for treatment for which a Govt servant or family member shall be entitled under Rule 11 shall be identical to the scale applicable to an official of the Indian Foreign Service of the corresponding grade in MEA under the Assisted Medical Attendance Scheme [Rule 11(11) GD]
  • GD(2) — Foreign exchange: Release of foreign exchange for treatment abroad — processed through MEA/RBI channels as per applicable foreign exchange regulations
  • GD(3) — Treatment in Nepal and Bhutan: Treatment in Nepal and Bhutan — special provisions as these are considered "abroad" for CS(MA) purposes but have special arrangement
  • GD(4) — Emergency abroad: If Govt servant falls ill abroad (on duty) — treatment abroad can be availed; reimbursement processed through CG's discretionary power under Rule 11(7)
Hinglish — Rule 11
🗣️ Hinglish — Rule 11
  • Bahar desh mein ilaj → Standing Committee se prior approval MANDATORY
  • Standing Committee check karti hai: kya yeh treatment India mein available nahi? Serious case hai?
  • Application: Ministry/Dept through → Standing Committee form mein
  • List review ho sakti hai: Government add/delete kar sakti hai approved treatments
  • Emergency (already abroad → suddenly beemar) → CG discretion se reimbursement possible without prior approval [Rule 11(7)]
⚠️ Exam Traps — Rule 11
  • "Treatment abroad without prior approval is always denied" — WRONG! Rule 11(7): CG may authorize even without prior approval in genuine emergencies
  • "Any treatment can be done abroad" — WRONG! Only specified conditions in the Table to Rule 11(3)
  • "Employee applies directly to Standing Committee" — WRONG! Application through Ministry/Department to Standing Committee
  • "The list of treatments for Rule 11 is permanent" — WRONG! Rule 11(4): Government can add or delete by notification
  • "Family members cannot go abroad for treatment under Rule 11" — WRONG! Family members are also covered

📜 M.2 — Annual Re-verification of AMA Appointment
  • Annual re-verification of doctors appointed as AMA under CS(MA) Rules is mandatory [MoHFW OM — see mohfw.gov.in/csma]
  • Process: Each year, the HoD or designated officer must reverify that the appointed AMA continues to be qualified, active, and suitable
  • Reverification: (a) The AMA must still be within 5 km if that was the basis; (b) AMA's qualifications/registration must still be valid; (c) AMA is still willing to serve as AMA
  • A fresh police verification may be done periodically (at least once in 5 years or as prescribed)

📜 M.3 — Hospital Empanelment under CS(MA) Rules
  • Who can be empanelled: Only private hospitals in non-CGHS covered cities considered for empanelment under CS(MA) Rules [MoHFW restriction — 2018 onwards]
  • Empanelment authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) has the power to recognize private hospitals
  • Guidelines: "Guidelines for recognition of Hospital under CS(MA) Rules, 1944" — available on MoHFW website
  • Dental hospitals: "Guidelines for Empanelment of Dental Hospital/Clinic" — separate guidelines
  • Eye hospitals: "Guidelines for Empanelment of private Eye hospitals/clinics under CS(MA) Rules 1944" — separate guidelines
  • NABH/NABL accreditation: NABH/NABL accreditation of hospitals/diagnostic centers recognized as AMA under CS(MA) is encouraged/mandated [MoHFW OM]
  • State-wise empanelled hospitals: Lists available on MoHFW website — State-wise (Haryana, MP, Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, UP, HP, Odisha, etc.)
  • CS(MA) beneficiaries at CGHS empanelled hospitals: CS(MA) beneficiaries and family members can get treatment at CGHS rates from any CGHS-empanelled HCO [MoHFW OM 11.01.2011] — this effectively extends access beyond just CS(MA)-empanelled hospitals
  • Annual Medical Examination hospitals: Separate list of recognized hospitals for Group A officers' annual medical examination under CS(MA) — available on MoHFW website
