🆕 UPDATE — HoD delegation — OM 16.02.2026 verified

Text of OM File No. S.11030/4/2026-EHS(8385264)/I/3840089/2026 dated 16.02.2026 verified: the ceiling for Heads of Departments of Ministries/Departments to settle medical-reimbursement cases (no relaxation of CGHS/CS(MA) Rules, entitlement strictly per prescribed rate lists) rises from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh without IFD consultation (earlier Rs.2 lakh → Rs.5 lakh by OM No. 11011/20/2014-CGHS(P)/EHS dated 23.11.2016); IFD concurrence CD No. 3131 dated 29.01.2026. This is the limit for HoDs of Ministries/Departments (serving employees under CGHS or CS(MA)); the CGHS administration’s own powers for pensioners and other beneficiaries are in OM 25.06.2026.

Read from the published text of the OM.

🆕 UPDATE — CS(MA) delegation to HoDs — OM 05.06.2014 (permissions, emergencies, limit)

MoHFW OM No. S.14025/01/2014-MS dated 05.06.2014 (IFD concurrence CD No. 335 dated 28.05.2014) — delegation to Heads of Departments for CS(MA) beneficiaries. Read in a Department of Posts letter of 25.11.2021 that reproduces it

  • A serving employee covered under CS(MA) who is being treated at a Government hospital and wants treatment in a private hospital recognised under CGHS / CS(MA): the Head of Department may grant permission for indoor treatment on the prescription of the concerned AMA.
  • Heads of Departments may decide reimbursement of emergency treatment at a private hospital / nursing home / clinic, subject to item-wise ceiling as per CGHS / CS(MA) rates.
  • Departments / Ministries settle all cases with no relaxation of rules where entitlement is worked out from the prescribed rate list: Heads up to Rs.2,00,000; above that (still per rate list) in consultation with the Internal Finance Division; only cases needing relaxation of rules go to MoHFW.

The letter adds that MoHFW (ID No. S.14025/35/2021-EHS dated 29.10.2021) clarified that the 2014 OM remains valid for CS(MA) beneficiaries, and that the Rs.5 lakh enhancement of OM 23.11.2016 was noted as applying to CGHS beneficiary cases. OM 16.02.2026 now sets the HoD ceiling at Rs.10 lakh for settlement “under CGHS or CS(MA) Rules”.

Read from the Department of Posts letter reproducing the OM — relayed text.

🆕 UPDATE — Medical advance where no package rate exists (OM 22.09.2021)

MoHFW OM No. Z.15025/8/2021/DIR/CGHS (signed 22.09.2021) — medical advance where no package rate is prescribed (refers to OM No. 14025/18/2015-MS/EHSS dated 17.10.2016: 90% advance for all treatment, OPD and IPD):

  • Admissible amount is computed item-wise at CGHS rates; for items with no CGHS rate, AIIMS rates; if there is none, the actual estimate.
  • The hospital seeking the advance must give an item-wise break-up of the estimate; 90% of the admissible amount so arrived at is advanced.
  • Other terms of the 17.10.2016 OM are unchanged.

🔄 HoD Delegation — CGHS OM 16.02.2026 (Also Applicable to CS(MA) Cases)

Delegation of Powers to HoDs for settling Permission cases and Post Facto Approval relating to Referral System and Medical Reimbursement under CGHS or CS(MA) Rules — speeds up processing significantly.

➕ Added [verified — File No. S.11030/4/2026-EHS(8385264), dated 16.02.2026]: This OM's core content is the enhancement of the HoD settlement ceiling from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh — HoDs can now settle medical reimbursement cases up to Rs.10,00,000 (where no relaxation of rules is involved and entitlement is worked out strictly per prescribed CGHS/CS(MA) rates) without IFD consultation. This supersedes the earlier ceiling of Rs.5 lakh fixed vide OM No.11011/20/2014-CGHS(P)/EHS dated 23.11.2016 (which itself had enhanced an original Rs.2 lakh ceiling). This Rs.10 lakh ceiling applies to ALL medical reimbursement claims — whether permission cases or post-facto approvals — where no relaxation of rules is involved and entitlement is worked out per prescribed CGHS/CS(MA) rates.

Hinglish — Advance & Claims
🗣️ Hinglish — Advance & Claims
  • CS(MA) claim deadline = 6 months — CGHS ka bhi ab 6 months hai (OM 01.06.2020).
  • Advance: IPD ke liye 90% CGHS rates. OPD ke liye bhi 90% agar estimate >Rs.10,000. TB ke liye 80% ya Rs.36K — jo kam ho.
  • Advance liya → hospital se discharge → 1 mahine mein final claim do.
  • Rejection → 45 din mein Central Government ko appeal.
  • HoD can settle cases now [2026 OM] — without going to MoHFW for routine cases.
⚠️ Critical Exam Trap
  • "CS(MA) claims within 3 months" — ABSOLUTELY WRONG! CS(MA) = 6 months; CGHS is also 6 months (OM 01.06.2020)
  • "IPD advance = 80%" — WRONG! IPD = 90%; TB with long treatment = 80%
  • "When advance drawn, final claim within 3 months" — WRONG! When advance drawn = 1 month from discharge
  • "Appeal to MoHFW within 45 days" — WRONG! Appeal to Central Government within 45 days

🆕 UPDATE — CS(MA) family: critical / terminal illness (OM 01.09.2026) & DA 63%

Dependent sons / brothers with critical or terminal illness may be covered for life (assessment by DGHS for CS(MA)); marriage does not end coverage in those cases; “family” is not expanded to his spouse / children. DA is 63% from 01.07.2026, so Rs.9,000 + DA ≈ Rs.14,670.

20.09.2023OM No. S.11025/18/2023-EHSRevised AMA consultation/injection fees: Specialist Rs.350; MBBS Rs.200; No separate day/night charges. Supersedes all earlier fee orders.
28.03.2024OM No. S.14025/15/2024-EHSExtension of parents/parents-in-law choice to CS(MA) beneficiaries — at par with CGHS. Both male and female employees can choose EITHER parents OR parents-in-law.

13.05.2026OM No. S.14025/15/2024-EHS(8270534)/I/3862000/2026Parents/parents-in-law choice: ONE-TIME IRREVOCABLE for male employees.   • Sep 2025: Transgender dependent children/siblings bhi covered — any age — Transgender Act 2019 certificate chahiye.
  • Feb 2026: HoD ko aur powers mili — permission cases CS(MA) mein bhi directly settle kar sakte hain.
  • May 2026 (LATEST): Parents ya parents-in-law ka choice ek baar hi milega — life bhar ke liye final. Maa-baap choose kar liye → sas-sasur nahi aayenge kabhi (even if parents expire).
⚠️ Critical Traps — Latest Amendments
  • "AMA specialist first consultation = Rs.100" — WRONG! Now Rs.350 [OM 20.09.2023]
  • "Parents/parents-in-law option was always available for CS(MA)" — WRONG! Extended to CS(MA) only in March 2024
  • "Parents-in-law option for male CS(MA) employees can be reversed" — WRONG! One-time irrevocable [OM 13.05.2026]
  • "Transgender dependents under CS(MA) must be below 25" — WRONG! Any age [Amendment 16.09.2025]
  • "CS(MA) beneficiary can avail treatment only at CS(MA)-empanelled hospitals" — WRONG! Can also use CGHS-empanelled hospitals at CGHS rates [OM 11.01.2011]

24"TB patient alone: half fare"Quarter fare

29"Night AMA consultation = extra charge"No extra for night — uniform rate [OM 20.09.2023]
30"MBBS AMA first consultation = Rs.350"MBBS = Rs.200 (Specialist/PG = Rs.350)
31"CS(MA) claim = 3 months"CS(MA) = 6 months (CGHS is also 6 months since OM 01.06.2020)
32"Emergency non-empanelled hospital: NABH rates"Non-NABH rates of nearest CGHS city

34"Family can get eyesight tested"Only employee; once in 3 years [Government Decision / OM under Rule 8(2)]
35"Spectacles covered at Govt expense"Only TESTING covered; spectacles NOT covered
36"Annual exam for all Govt servants"Only Group A, age 40+ [Government Decision / OM under Rule 8(2)]
37"Annual exam: men Rs.2,200"Men = Rs.2,000; Women = Rs.2,200 [Government Decision / OM under Rule 8(2)]

39"Cochlear = Rs.3 lakh"Rs.7,00,000 (pre-lingual) / Rs.6,00,000 (post-lingual), incl. GST [OM 09.11.2026] [Government Decision / OM under Rule 8(2)]
40"AICD covered under stent/pacemaker provision"AICD excluded specifically
41"Stents: 2 max per patient"Maximum 3 stents; costliest DES ceiling Rs.29,000 [OM 24.03.2023]

Additional Rules

Insurance Claims, Pensioner Exclusion, Foundational OMs & Special Charges

OM 11.01.2011 (Two-source) | OM 29.09.2016 (Pensioners) | OM 18.04.1945 (Foundation)
📜 R.1 — Two-Source Reimbursement (Insurance + Department)
  • Beneficiaries with a private medical insurance policy can claim from both the insurer and the Department.
  • Condition: The total amount reimbursed from both sources must not exceed the actual expenditure incurred.
  • Process: Beneficiary must first claim from the insurance company. After getting the settlement, the remaining amount (up to CGHS/CS(MA) rates) can be claimed from the Department by providing insurance settlement summary.
📜 R.2 — Non-Applicability to Pensioners
  • CS(MA) Rules, 1944 are NOT applicable to pensioners [MoHFW OM dated 29.09.2016].
  • Pensioners in CGHS areas must register with CGHS.
  • Pensioners in non-CGHS areas have the option of FMA (Rs.3,000) or subscribing to CGHS for OPD/IPD benefits.
📜 R.3 — Foundational History & Scope
  • Extension to Families [18.04.1945]: Medical concessions under CS(MA) were extended to families of Central Govt servants shortly after the main rules.
  • Modern Medicine Only [06.11.1961]: Originally, only the Allopathic system was recognized; AYUSH systems were incorporated later through specific OMs following CGHS lines.
  • State/District Restrictions: Restrictions on taking treatment in hospitals outside the home State or District have been removed [MoHFW OM].
Hinglish — Additional Rules
🗣️ Hinglish — Additional Rules
  • Insurance + Office: Dono se paise le sakte ho, par total bill se zyada nahi. Pehle insurance se lo, fir bacha hua office se claim karo.
  • Pensioners: CS(MA) rules unpe laagu nahi hote. Unko CGHS ya FMA lena hota hai.
  • Allopathy: CS(MA) ka main system modern medicine (Allopathy) hai, par AYUSH bhi allowed hai limited cases mein.

🎓 Superintendent (NIT / IIT) exam map & claim processing

🎓 What this means for preparation

No syllabus I could open names sub-topics: it says only “CGHS/CS(MA) Rules” or “Medical Attendance rules”. So expect questions at the level of entitlement, definitions (AMA, family), who may authorise, time limits, advance, reimbursement rates and recent orders, and — for a Superintendent — checking a claim against the rules. Everything in this guide is limited to official CGHS and CS(MA) rules and orders. Use the mock tests (case scenarios) and the Memory sheet, and confirm the topic list in your advertisement.

1 · What the syllabi say

Syllabus wording found (sources: institute recruitment notifications)
Recruiting instituteWhat the syllabus says about these rulesWeight / note
NIT Warangal (Examination Syllabus, 2025)“… Purchase procedures, Tendering process, Contract Management, CGHS/CS(MA) Rules, General Accounting Procedures, PFMS …” in the 60-question domain-knowledge portionSuperintendent Stage-I: 100 objective questions, 200 marks (2 each), 0.5 marks deducted per wrong answer, 2 hours; 40 general + 60 domain; 6 × vacancies shortlisted. CGHS/CS(MA) is one of 30+ domain items (so expect only a few questions — my inference)
MANIT Bhopal and SVNIT Surat (Superintendent syllabus)“… CCS (LTC) rules, Medical Attendance rules, RTI Act-2005, CCS Pension Rules 1972 …”One item in a long list; no sub-topics named
IIT Bhubaneswar (Junior Superintendent paper, 2013 — old)“GFR-2005, GPF, CPF, EPF, NPS, CCS (Pension) Rules 1972, CGHS, CS (MA) Rules [15 questions]”Weight 15 shared with the pension / GPF topics; may have changed since
NIT Raipur advertisement, 2026 (search summary only — document not opened)Search summary lists CGHS/CS(MA) Rules in the indicative domain syllabusCheck the advertisement for your exam

🔎 Verify list

Items that need a second look before you rely on them in an exam answer. Nothing here changes the rule text — it only flags dynamic figures, internally inconsistent cross-references and statements that cite no order number.

Flagged by reading the guide

Rule 4 — fare concession
The Rule 4 body gives “Patient + Attendant: half of normal fare / Patient alone: one quarter” without naming the category, while the Rule 4 trap list says “TB patient + attendant: half fare”. Confirm the category against the primary text before relying on it.
Rule 4
Rule 11 — cross-reference
Rule 11 GD(1) cites “[Rule 11(11) GD]” although the section describes sub-rules (1)–(7). Treat the cross-reference as unverified.
Rule 11
Distance wording
Rule 4 uses “five miles (≈ 8 km)”. AMA-appointment GD(1) says “5 kms (8 km by some references)”. The two distance tests are different rules — do not mix them.
Rule 2(a) / Rule 4
CS(MA) mix-ups
Several CS(MA) sections point to “see mohfw.gov.in/csma” with no OM number (AMA re-verification, NABH/NABL accreditation, AYAH/nursing ceiling). The guide does not give the order number — check before quoting in an answer.
Rule 2(a) GD, Rule 8

Still unverified

Recent CGHS / CS(MA) orders (Jan–Nov 2026) were read in full — see the Latest orders tab. What could not be confirmed:

UnverifiedAMA appointment — OM number
The guide says the Head of Department appoints private practitioners as AMA (Rule 2(a) GD(2)) but cites no OM number. The CS(MA) Rules PDF and the MoHFW CS(MA) page (orders list, AMA re-verification OM, verification proforma) could not be opened from this environment (HTTP 502). A CSIR policy document found in search says Supplementary Rule 2(10) allows a private registered practitioner to be appointed AMA for a class of employees where adequate doctors are unavailable — consistent with the guide, but not read at the source.
UnverifiedPensioners’ emergency claims
The guide says emergency claims within prescribed rates for pensioners are settled by the Head of the CGHS-covered city with no financial limit. OM 25.06.2026 gives the Additional Director / Director / AS&DG financial powers for CGHS claims generally and does not mention an “emergency, no limit” category; treat the “no limit” statement for pensioners as unconfirmed.
UnverifiedPre-16.02.2026 statements
Statements in older sections that quote “Rs.5 lakh” for the HoD / IFD threshold have already been corrected in the guide; if you see one elsewhere, Rs.10 lakh (OM 16.02.2026) is the current HoD figure.
UnverifiedSource of the 2026 orders
Every 2026 order and correction in this guide was read from a copy of the official OM hosted on staffnews.in, not on mohfw.gov.in. On 26.11.2026 the legacy MoHFW host (main.mohfw.gov.in) failed at the proxy (502) and the new site (www.mohfw.gov.in) had an empty document store. Before quoting a figure in an answer, confirm it against the MoHFW CS(MA) page or the CGHS site.
UnverifiedPsychiatry consultation rate
The guide (OM 12.04.2023 table) lists “Super-specialty / Psychiatry consultation Rs.700”. OM 13.01.2026 says Rs.700 is admissible only for DM / MCh super specialists in their discipline; whether psychiatry consultations by non-DM/MCh psychiatrists still attract Rs.700 was not found in a primary text. Treat the “psychiatry” part as unconfirmed.
UnverifiedCGHS 6-month claim limit
Based on CGHS OM File No. 1-60/2017-CGHS/C&P/EHS (01.06.2020), read in full; no later revision was found. The original guide’s “CGHS 3 months / CS(MA) 6 months” statements were replaced. Confirm on the CGHS site, because a later circular may exist that was not published on the sites searched.
UnverifiedHoD limit for CS(MA) before 2026
A Department of Posts letter (25.11.2021) relays MoHFW’s clarification that the Rs.2 lakh OM of 05.06.2014 stays valid for CS(MA) and that the Rs.5 lakh step of 23.11.2016 was noted for CGHS beneficiary cases. The guide’s single history line (Rs.2L → 5L → 10L) may therefore not describe CS(MA) before 2026. Since OM 16.02.2026 the Rs.10 lakh limit is stated for “CGHS or CS(MA) Rules”.
UnverifiedSyllabus sources
NIT Warangal (2025) pattern was read for the Superintendent post. NIT Raipur 2026 is quoted from a search summary only. The IIT Bhubaneswar paper is from 2013. Always check the advertisement for your exam.
UnverifiedOrders after 09.11.2026
The search for new orders was made on 25.11.2026. Anything issued later, or not published on the sites searched, is not included.
